nodes.label: volsync-mover-nfs MutatingAdmissionPolicy injects the per-cluster repository mount
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: volsync-mover-nfs mutatingadmissionpolicy injects the per-cluster repository mount
nodes.rationale: RESTIC_REPOSITORY renders as the in-container path /repository/${APP}, which looks cluster-global; the actual filesystem location comes from an admission policy that mounts nfs path /mnt/stash/backup/${CLUSTER_CNAME}/volsync onto every volsync-* mover Job. CLUSTER_CNAME arrives via the cluster-secrets substitution patch injected by the root cluster-apps Kustomization.

nodes.label: RUNBOOK Scenario B — the break-glass standby is a procedure, not a command
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: runbook scenario b — the break-glass standby is a procedure, not a command
nodes.rationale: bao-standby is deliberately stopped by default (compose --profile break-glass) so alpha-site does not permanently co-locate the transit-seal key with a live copy of everything it protects; the nightly dump also carries an age layer so possession of alpha-site alone is not enough. The monthly restore drill proves the dump restores into a scratch sidecar, not that a real pulumi preview can run against the standby — so the exit gate is a one-time rehearsal with BAO_ADDR pointed at the standby, then standing it back down.

nodes.label: Eight ungated OnePasswordItem dual-writes
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.rationale: Nine call sites still write 1Password items on every apply; only the PBS one lacks an OpenBao mirror. Unlike OpenBao writes (gated by baoDualWriteEnabled) there is no 1Password dual-write gate — open question whether that redundancy is intentional.

nodes.label: ClusterDefinition
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.rationale: A single record (type, key, title, rootDomain, authentikDomain, secret, icon) drives DNS, Traefik, Authentik and UI branding per cluster, so adding a cluster is a data change rather than a code change.

nodes.label: ComponentResource pattern
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.rationale: Reusable infrastructure is expressed as classes with children parented to `this` and outputs registered via registerOutputs, so a child (e.g. DockgeLxc) can reach its parent's provider rather than constructing its own.

nodes.label: GlobalResources (central provider + credential wiring)
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.rationale: Every stack constructs GlobalResources first; it initializes all providers from credentials fetched at construction time, so a stack never has to know how a credential is obtained.

nodes.label: OPClient (1Password Connect client)
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.rationale: Fetches 1Password items by title; the guide presents it as the single read path for credentials, which the OpenBao migration later inverted (reads moved to BaoStore, OPClient became write-only).

nodes.label: shared/cloudflare-driscoll-tech is the estate's designated canary
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: shared/cloudflare-driscoll-tech is the estate's designated canary
nodes.rationale: Three non-ESO consumers read it in lockstep: openbao-replica's CANARY_PATH health check (with the KV v2 data/ infix), bao-standby's restore.sh break-glass read, and components/globals.ts's Cloudflare provider. Recommendation: KEEP the path where it is.

nodes.label: Home Operations Development Guide
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)

nodes.label: PITR is available-but-unrehearsed on both clusters
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: pitr is available-but-unrehearsed on both clusters
nodes.rationale: The NoSuchBucket archiving failure was fixed and both clusters show 10 consecutive completed daily backups with a real recovery window, but nobody has restored into a scratch cluster and timed it — 'restores are rehearsed, not improvised'. So PITR is additive margin and does not replace the nightly logical dump each CNPG-touching step must still take.

nodes.label: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: the openbao catch-22 (globalresources cannot construct without a live openbao)
nodes.rationale: GlobalResources builds a BaoStore and makes seven getSecretByTitle calls before any stack code runs, on preview as well as up. OpenBao itself runs inside equestria (3-pod HA StatefulSet on the shared CNPG postgres) and is transit-sealed from alpha-site, so 'both clusters down' and 'OpenBao down' are nearly the same event.

nodes.label: Not to be confused with OpenBao's Postgres
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: not to be confused with openbao's postgres
nodes.rationale: This piece's database is celestia's Docker-hosted Postgres reached over Tailscale; OpenBao's is the shared CNPG cluster inside equestria. Routing Pulumi state through the CNPG cluster would recreate the exact fate-sharing problem, just against equestria instead of spike.

nodes.label: Two never-re-keyed SOPS files (the undecryptable-window trap)
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: two never-re-keyed sops files (the undecryptable-window trap)
nodes.rationale: .sops.yaml records POLICY, not whether each file was actually re-encrypted after the policy changed. Two SGC files (talsecret.sops.yaml, flux-instance/secret.sops.yaml) were never updatekeys'd and do not carry equestria's recipient — narrowing to one recipient first would make them permanently undecryptable. Run sops updatekeys on them while SGC's private key can still decrypt them, then audit every sops footer for the surviving recipient before touching any .sops.yaml.
nodes.source_location: The trap this plan almost inherited

nodes.label: The authentik stack must be host-scoped, not _common
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: the authentik stack must be host-scoped, not _common
nodes.rationale: DockgeLxc.deployStacks builds each host's stack list as the union of docker/_common/* and docker/<host>/*, so a _common placement would deploy authentik to every Dockge host. It also cannot carry an `authentik:` self-provisioning block in its own definition.yaml — authentik cannot be an OAuth client of itself.

nodes.label: Provider centralization rule
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.rationale: All providers are created in exactly one place (GlobalResources). Duplicating a provider inside a stack splits credential/state handling and is called out as 'NEVER DO THIS'.

nodes.label: concealed_fields custom metadata must carry over
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: concealed_fields custom metadata must carry over
nodes.rationale: shapeItem throws on a path marked contains_secrets: true with no concealed_fields, and a path that silently loses the list downgrades every value to plaintext in Pulumi state — secrecy comes from custom_metadata, not from the value itself.

nodes.label: KV v2 has no rename — copy, repoint, verify, then metadata delete
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: kv v2 has no rename — copy, repoint, verify, then metadata delete
nodes.rationale: Moving a path means write-new → repoint consumers → verify → delete-old. Always copy the value, never regenerate: a new crypto-key or secret-key makes stored data unreadable and a new session key logs everyone out.

nodes.label: resolveBaoPath: title-addressed reads do not follow the data
nodes.community_name: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: resolvebaopath: title-addressed reads do not follow the data
nodes.rationale: components/store/bao.ts derives shared/<baoSlug(title)> from a 1Password-style title, so eight paths are addressed by title with no literal 'shared/...' string in the repo. Moving one of those requires editing the call site to getSecretByPath(...) — moving the data alone turns into a hard throw.

nodes.label: vault#127 — etcd fsync starvation on fluttershy/kerfuffle PNY SATA disks
nodes.norm_label: vault#127 — etcd fsync starvation on fluttershy/kerfuffle pny sata disks
nodes.rationale: Those nodes install /var (and therefore etcd) on a 27ms-write-latency SATA SSD while the fast NVMe is fully allocated to Longhorn; a write-heavy pod (pulumi Workspace, ~71% of the disk load) pushes etcd past its 10ms p99 fsync budget and cascades into cluster-wide leader-election losses. The durable fix is piece 19 turning those nodes into workers, so the interim mitigation is only a nodeSelector pinning Workspace pods away.

nodes.label: Break-glass SOPS artifact set in bootstrap/openbao
nodes.norm_label: break-glass sops artifact set in bootstrap/openbao
nodes.rationale: Seven files (static-unseal, transit-token, pulumi-approle, pulumi-passphrase, recovery-keys, break-glass-approle, restore-test-approle) each unlock exactly one link of the chain; all are decryptable only by the estate age.key, and each must be sops --decrypt tested from a machine that is not alpha-site.

nodes.label: CONNECT_HOST repoint from op-connect.sgc to op-connect.equestria
nodes.norm_label: connect_host repoint from op-connect.sgc to op-connect.equestria
nodes.rationale: A two-line change in two repos' .config/mise.toml. It still matters because nine call sites still construct live OnePasswordItem writes, so Connect reachability is load-bearing for more than a human LXC login — but it is now a write-path concern only, not a read dependency.

nodes.label: Two independent OpenBao auth paths inside one pulumi preview
nodes.norm_label: two independent openbao auth paths inside one pulumi preview
nodes.rationale: BaoClient does its own lazy AppRole login off BAO_ADDR/ROLE_ID/SECRET_ID inside the program; vals runs BEFORE Pulumi to resolve ref+openbao:// literals in mise's [env] and cannot do an AppRole exchange, so it needs a pre-minted VAULT_TOKEN. pulumi-env.sh feeds both from one SOPS-encrypted AppRole.

nodes.label: system/backups backend prefix mismatch
nodes.rationale: The system Stack CR points the operator at s3://home-operations/backups while stacks/system/.mise.toml points local runs at s3://home-operations/system — every other stack agrees with itself. In-cluster and local runs therefore write two different state locations, and migrating the wrong one silently loses the clusters/* outputs every other stack reads.

nodes.label: skystar as proposed test target (recommended, not decided)
nodes.norm_label: skystar as proposed test target (recommended, not decided)
nodes.rationale: A Dockge cluster on its own Proxmox host, so testing there cannot touch equestria or SGC by accident — and it is none of the three hosts this plan is rewiring. Caveat the discovery undersells: skystar already runs backrest, backups/rclone-sftp and a PBS instance, so it is the offsite backup replication target, not an empty box. Its slowest-measured write latency is irrelevant to test-target fitness and must not be mistaken for disqualification.

nodes.label: OIDC auth method moved from equestria-init.sh into components/openbao/oidc.ts
nodes.norm_label: oidc auth method moved from equestria-init.sh into components/openbao/oidc.ts
nodes.rationale: The viewer policy, the oidc JWT auth backend and the admin/family roles became vault.Policy / vault.jwt.AuthBackend(Role) wired into stacks/home. The real win is that the Authentik client credentials produced by the applications stack are read directly by Pulumi instead of a human copying client_id/secret/issuer into env vars for a one-shot script.

nodes.label: 03 — Secrets bootstrap independence
nodes.rationale: Goal: a local pulumi preview succeeds from a laptop with both clusters powered off. The framing inverted since the issue was opened — the catch-22 is now OpenBao-shaped, not 1Password-shaped.

nodes.label: 04 — Pulumi state backend: Minio-on-truenas → Postgres DIY on celestia
nodes.norm_label: 04 — pulumi state backend: minio-on-truenas → postgres diy on celestia
nodes.rationale: Ten Stack CRs move off the s3:// backend to postgres:// DIY; Minio is retained as a versioned stack-export archive rather than decommissioned, because the Postgres backend still carries the [PREVIEW] label and deserves a documented path back.

nodes.label: 05 — Import audit
nodes.rationale: Every permanent `import:` resource option must be proven safe or removed before the DNS-heavy phases lean on this code path. Most of the acute risk turns out to already be closed.

nodes.label: PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE moved into OpenBao (one chain, not two)
nodes.norm_label: pulumi_config_passphrase moved into openbao (one chain, not two)
nodes.rationale: Before 2026-08-12 the state passphrase was a SOPS-only secret independent of OpenBao; now it is age key → sops → AppRole → OpenBao like everything else, with a break-glass SOPS copy kept for when OpenBao is unreachable. Simpler to reason about, but no secret is exempt from 'OpenBao must be reachable' any more — including the one that decrypts Pulumi's own state.

nodes.label: celestia over alpha-site for the state backend
nodes.norm_label: celestia over alpha-site for the state backend
nodes.rationale: 'You can put identity on the Pi, or state on the Pi, but not both.' Concentrating the artifact needed to rebuild everything onto the box used for risky experiments — and, after piece 07, also holding SSO — would repeat the spike-concentration mistake this piece exists to fix.

nodes.label: Spike single-machine fate-sharing (the actual argument for the move)
nodes.norm_label: spike single-machine fate-sharing (the actual argument for the move)
nodes.rationale: One TrueNAS VM hosts the Pulumi state bucket, the VolSync restic repo, the nfs-csi share, the Thanos bucket and the PBS datastore mount — and no backup plan references the Minio dataset. If spike is what is being rebuilt, the estate has neither the state nor a backup of it. Moving state into Postgres puts it inside the existing pg_dump → backrest → PBS chain automatically.

nodes.label: mise [env] re-application clobbers hand-exported variables
nodes.rationale: ref+openbao:// values are deliberately left unresolved in the environment (mise re-evaluates [env] per shell load with no caching), so the real entrypoint is the .config/mise/tasks/vals-run task. Exporting a variable by hand and then calling mise run does not protect it — the .mise.toml value can win — so a smoke test must run from outside the repo tree or edit the .mise.toml itself.

nodes.label: The aborted cutover and the gate it earned
nodes.norm_label: the aborted cutover and the gate it earned
nodes.rationale: Steps 2-3 hold; steps 4-5 did not, because the estate's Pulumi state backend was broken for hours (pulumi-nodejs 3.257.0 'Invalid checksum provided' against Minio) without anyone noticing. The DNS names had already been released from SGC and then re-claimed, leaving both sides claiming them. New precondition: confirm stacks/home can complete a run BEFORE releasing any name from SGC — the release half is cheap to do and slow to undo. Also: the restored database ages from the moment it lands, so any retry re-runs the dump.

nodes.label: Nothing else new lands on this Pi
nodes.norm_label: nothing else new lands on this pi
nodes.rationale: alpha-site already hosts bao-transit (the sole unseal path for equestria's OpenBao) and bao-standby (the DR receiver) — neither existed when the July concentration-risk analysis was written. With authentik added, re-measured headroom is ~1.2-1.7 GiB, so the rule is load-bearing rather than advisory.

nodes.label: An adjacent answer is not a confirmation
nodes.norm_label: an adjacent answer is not a confirmation
nodes.rationale: David's reply reaffirmed alpha-site as the identity host (a decision already settled) rather than answering where the test-target designation should move. Every other item in the same list got a direct answer; this one did not, so it must be asked explicitly rather than inferred.

nodes.label: The bootstrap dividing line (what can never become a Pulumi resource)
nodes.norm_label: the bootstrap dividing line (what can never become a pulumi resource)
nodes.rationale: Pulumi authenticates to OpenBao with a token, so anything required to make that token exist (operator init, recovery-share handling, root-token regeneration, the pulumi AppRole) cannot be a Pulumi resource — it would be a resource in the system it is bootstrapping. Everything after the first working token is fair game.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: csi-driver-nfs
nodes.rationale: Storage-driver release hardened for churn: 7 install/upgrade retries with rollback strategy, CRDs CreateReplace, recreate on rollback — a CSI driver that fails to converge takes every PVC in the cluster with it.

nodes.label: HelmRepository: csi-driver-nfs
nodes.rationale: Points straight at the upstream kubernetes-csi GitHub raw charts directory rather than an OCI mirror, unlike the observability apps in this repo which use ghcr.io charts-mirror OCIRepositories.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: csi-driver-nfs
nodes.rationale: wait: true because downstream PVC-consuming apps must not reconcile before the NFS driver is healthy; depends on onepassword-connect and external-secrets so the SPIKE_IP substitution chain is available.

nodes.label: ConfigMap generator: csi-driver-nfs-values
nodes.rationale: disableNameSuffixHash: true so the HelmRelease can reference a stable ConfigMap name in valuesFrom; the tradeoff is that values changes do not roll the release by name change alone.

nodes.label: StorageClass: nfs-csi
nodes.rationale: reclaimPolicy Retain protects the /mnt/stash share from PVC deletion; NFS 4.2 with nconnect=8 and hard mounts trades hung-on-outage behaviour for throughput and no silent I/O errors. Server address comes from the ${SPIKE_IP} substitution.

nodes.label: csi-driver-nfs chart values
nodes.rationale: mountPermissions 0 defers permission control to the NFS export; the controller disables its own snapshotter but enables externalSnapshotter, so snapshot CRs are served by the shared external component rather than a per-driver sidecar.

nodes.label: nfs-system namespace kustomization
nodes.rationale: pod-security enforce: privileged is required because CSI node plugins mount host paths and run privileged; pulls in the shared alerts and common components for every app in the namespace.

nodes.label: ConfigMap generator: alloy-configmap
nodes.rationale: Generates key config.alloy from ./resources/config.alloy with disableNameSuffixHash so the HelmRelease can name it statically; the reloader annotation on the controller is what actually propagates changes.

nodes.rationale: Applications are created from Kubernetes CRDs (ApplicationDefinition, ClusterDefinition) rather than being enumerated in code, so adding an app to a cluster is a cluster-side change; the same component mints OAuth2 client IDs/secrets and wires the per-cluster outposts.

nodes.rationale: Reads ApplicationDefinition/ClusterDefinition CRDs plus ConfigMaps and Secrets, and manages kubeconfigs for remote clusters so one Authentik install can serve outposts on several clusters.

nodes.norm_label: 1password secret integration for the authentik stack
nodes.rationale: The C# original used a native OnePassword Pulumi provider; the TypeScript port deliberately reuses the repo's existing OPClient from components/op.ts instead of adding a second 1Password access path.

nodes.label: authentik stack (Pulumi project: applications)
nodes.rationale: Declared project name is `applications`, not `authentik`. Per stacks/vault/Pulumi.yaml the project name is embedded in every resource URN, so the historical name is kept deliberately to avoid Pulumi treating the stack as a brand-new project and recreating/orphaning every resource.

nodes.label: authentik stack secrets encryptionsalt
nodes.rationale: Stack-settings file carries only an encryptionsalt: config secrets are passphrase-encrypted (PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE) rather than stored as plaintext, matching the repo safety rule that no plaintext credentials are committed.

nodes.label: Authentik Pulumi Stack (TypeScript)

nodes.label: vault stack (Pulumi project: applications)
nodes.rationale: Migrated from the david-driscoll/vault repo on 2026-08-22 with its state left at s3://home-operations/vault. The project name is part of every resource URN (urn:pulumi:vault::applications::...), so renaming it to `vault` would make Pulumi see a new project and recreate every TailnetKey, GitHub App token, Secret patch and webhook while orphaning the originals.

nodes.label: C#-to-TypeScript conversion of the Authentik project
nodes.norm_label: c#-to-typescript conversion of the authentik project
nodes.rationale: Port of stargate-command-cluster/pulumi/authentik from C#. Trade-offs called out: Mapperly object mapping must be hand-written in TypeScript, the tight Kubernetes integration must be redone with @pulumi/kubernetes or a K8s client, LINQ queries become array operations, and the native OnePassword provider is replaced by the repo's own OPClient. The document is internally inconsistent — it declares the conversion complete while also listing flows, stages, policies and application resources as still to be converted.

nodes.label: Node.js runtime with tsx/esm loader (no compile step)
nodes.norm_label: node.js runtime with tsx/esm loader (no compile step)
nodes.rationale: Every stack declares runtime nodejs with typescript:false and nodeargs `--import tsx/esm`. Pulumi therefore executes TypeScript directly through the tsx ESM loader instead of relying on Pulumi's built-in ts-node path, so no separate build/compile step exists and path aliases resolve at runtime.

nodes.label: Pulumi URN project-name stability constraint
nodes.rationale: A Pulumi project name is embedded in every resource URN, so changing it is equivalent to declaring a new project: all resources are re-created and the previous ones are orphaned in the estate. This is why three unrelated stack directories (authentik, unifi-network, vault) all declare the project name `applications`.

nodes.norm_label: the live literal import on the home-operations minio bucket
nodes.rationale: import: "home-operations" is a literal evaluated on every run, but the resource has no deleteBeforeReplace and does have protect: true, which refuses any delete without a manual unprotect — so the worst case is a loud protect error, not a silent live delete. Whether it re-imports every run is still unverified; the test is two consecutive previews with nothing else changing, because a single clean preview does not prove safety.

nodes.label: StandardDns imports are structurally inert (but the wire is still there)
nodes.community_name: import + deleteBeforeReplace with a mismatched id format
nodes.norm_label: standarddns imports are structurally inert (but the wire is still there)
nodes.rationale: unifiId and cloudflareId are hardcoded undefined inside the only public entry point (StandardDns.create), whose signature exposes no id parameter — so no caller can arm the bug today. Residual risk: the private constructor still threads those params into import: + deleteBeforeReplace, so a future edit could re-arm it. Recommended cleanup is deleting the dead parameters entirely.

nodes.label: Minio bucket protect + retainOnDelete
nodes.community_name: import + deleteBeforeReplace with a mismatched id format
nodes.rationale: protect: true refuses any delete without a manual unprotect, and retainOnDelete keeps data through a stack destroy — the guardrails the Pulumi state bucket relies on.

nodes.label: import + deleteBeforeReplace with a mismatched id format
nodes.community_name: import + deleteBeforeReplace with a mismatched id format
nodes.norm_label: import + deletebeforereplace with a mismatched id format
nodes.rationale: When the supplied import id can never equal what the provider stores back in state, every run re-plans the same replace; with deleteBeforeReplace the destroy runs first. Cloudflare (<zoneId>/<recordId> vs bare recordId) wiped all 56 managed DNS records twice; UniFi (<site>:<recordId> vs bare) destroyed nine. Both fixes reuse the Pulumi resource NAME so a collision becomes a same-name replacement rather than an import.

nodes.label: Keep the archive bucket Pulumi-managed
nodes.community_name: import + deleteBeforeReplace with a mismatched id format
nodes.rationale: protect + retainOnDelete only stay enforced and drift-checked while Pulumi manages the resource; unmanaging it moves the 'does this exist correctly' question outside the audit trail; and bucket versioning (minio.S3BucketVersioning) is only expressible as config if the resource stays managed.

Do NOT use the `import` resource option as a shortcut — the StandardDns/Cloudflare incident showed an id-format mismatch re-imports every run and, with deleteBeforeReplace, destroys live records.

Parsed by components/dockerStackPostgres.ts into the postgres stack's generated .env-local.

nodes.norm_label: externalname + tailnet-inbound proxygroup route to celestia postgres
nodes.rationale: The shared _common postgres publishes no ports and is reachable only from dockge_default, so both workspace pods and laptops are outside it. The fix reuses the existing kubeproxies pattern: an ExternalName Service annotated tailscale.com/tailnet-fqdn + proxy-group: tailnet-inbound, plus a tcp:5432 ACL grant modelled on the existing baoDumps tcp:2023 grant.

nodes.label: PGAPP_<NAME>_PASSWORD provisioning convention
nodes.rationale: One line in docker/<host>/postgres/.env-local becomes a login role plus an owned database on the next idempotent postgres-provision run, because DockgeLxc merges docker/_common/<stack>/ with docker/<host>/<stack>/ per relative path (host files win). Adding a database therefore needs zero changes in stacks/backups — the per-host backrest plan already covers /opt/stacks-data and postgres-backup already dumps every database.

nodes.label: ensure: absent tombstone (retain-by-default drop protocol)
nodes.rationale: Removing an entry never drops anything — retain is the default. Dropping a database requires declaring `ensure: absent`, deploying, and only then deleting the entry, so an accidental deletion from the file can never destroy data.

nodes.label: USB-SATA fsync/FUA test on sda (hard prerequisite)
nodes.norm_label: usb-sata fsync/fua test on sda (hard prerequisite)
nodes.rationale: node_disk_write_time_seconds_total measures request service time, not REQ_OP_FLUSH. USB-SATA/NVMe bridges either serialize fsync slowly or silently ignore FUA — the second is data loss on a power cut, not a latency number. This is a correctness signal that must be tested before Postgres lands, not optional due diligence.

nodes.label: Reuse the shared _common Postgres instead of a dedicated container
nodes.norm_label: reuse the shared _common postgres instead of a dedicated container
nodes.rationale: The generic shared-Postgres pattern did not exist on alpha-site in July; now it does, so declaring PGAPP_AUTHENTIK_PASSWORD gets the pg_dump → backrest → PBS chain for free as existing generic infrastructure, costs one fewer Postgres process on thin headroom, and one fewer thing to fsync-test and monitor. The restore half of the chain still has to be proven separately.

nodes.norm_label: baokvsecret sets retainondelete — old paths need hand-deletion

nodes.norm_label: trailing * in an openbao acl is a prefix glob (nesting is free)

A brand-new TOP-LEVEL prefix would need a grant in every eso-* policy plus the AppRole — an admin write, therefore a root ceremony. That asymmetry is the main reason to nest rather than invent prefixes.

nodes.norm_label: immich requires a superuser role that rotation preserves

A DatabaseRole ADOPTS an existing role and forces every attribute to match the manifest, so the attribute must be restated or the live role is silently demoted. It has to be a component rather than a substitution because booleans cannot pass through postBuild.substitute. immich was migrated last (tranche 9) to prove that OpenBao rotation issues only ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD, leaving rolsuper true and all 8 extensions intact.

nodes.rationale: The value is the master key of the Meilisearch instance karakeep points at, not karakeep's own secret. Meilisearch enforces auth now, so any other value is a 403 on every search. NEXTAUTH_SECRET is karakeep's own and is correctly unrelated.

nodes.community_name: The 2026-09-21 re-run: plugins, repositories and settings included
nodes.rationale: 314 lines of C# that walked every ks.yaml and spliced results into three central files. It existed only because before CNPG 1.30 there was no per-role custom resource — roles could only be declared inline in Cluster.spec.managed.roles. That constraint is gone.

nodes.label: Media Stack SQLite to PostgreSQL Migration
nodes.community_name: The 2026-09-21 re-run: plugins, repositories and settings included
nodes.norm_label: media stack sqlite to postgresql migration
nodes.rationale: Eight applications in two families onto the shared CNPG cluster. Most upstreams call the SQLite migration unsupported and mean it — the Servarr pages support only fresh installs and the Overseerr family routes through a community pgloader build from an unmerged PR — so the rollback is not a formality. Four more apps (kapowarr, mylar, sabnzbd, qbittorrent) were checked and have no relational database at all.

nodes.label: Component-Emitted ks Does Not Inherit components/common
nodes.community_name: The 2026-09-21 re-run: plugins, repositories and settings included
nodes.norm_label: component-emitted ks does not inherit components/common
nodes.rationale: ks.yaml files are collected by the umbrella kustomization, which is where components/common applies its decryption + substituteFrom: cluster-secrets patch. A component-emitted nested ks is built from the app path, so both must be written into the component's ks.yaml explicitly or ${CLUSTER_DOMAIN} silently fails to resolve.

nodes.label: Nested Flux Kustomization from a Component
nodes.community_name: The 2026-09-21 re-run: plugins, repositories and settings included
nodes.norm_label: nested flux kustomization from a component
nodes.rationale: Flux's spec.targetNamespace uses Kustomize's namespace transformer, which OVERRIDES an explicitly-set metadata.namespace — verified with a two-document fixture. So a component rendered inside an app's build cannot put Database/DatabaseRole in the `database` namespace; it must emit a nested ${APP}-postgres Kustomization with targetNamespace: database. wait: false and dependsOn: postgres-operator (not the postgres cluster ks) avoid the OpenBao/CNPG readiness cycle.
nodes.source_location: Why the component needs a nested Flux Kustomization

nodes.label: DatabaseRole Adoption Forces Every Attribute
nodes.community_name: The 2026-09-21 re-run: plugins, repositories and settings included
nodes.rationale: Creating a DatabaseRole for an existing role ADOPTS it and the operator forces every attribute to match the manifest, including omitted ones. Omitting superuser on immich would silently demote it, which is why ${POSTGRES_SUPERUSER:=false} is a substitution.

nodes.rationale: The GarageCluster CR is the identity of the object store: its StatefulSets, their PVCs and the Garage layout all hang off it, so ownership changes must orphan rather than cascade-delete.

nodes.label: wait:false so Low Power mode cannot stall dependents
nodes.norm_label: wait:false so low power mode cannot stall dependents
nodes.rationale: wait: true would block the Kustomization on GarageCluster reaching Ready, and Ready requires three schedulable bulk workers. In Low Power mode (D6) there are none, so the Kustomization would sit failing for the whole window and drag every dependent with it. Health is judged by the Gatus endpoint in definition.yaml instead.

nodes.label: cert-manager-controller is a hard prerequisite for admission
nodes.norm_label: cert-manager-controller is a hard prerequisite for admission
nodes.rationale: The chart's admission and conversion webhooks are on by default and their certificates come from cert-manager. Without the controller the HelmRelease installs a Certificate that never issues, the webhook Service has no serving cert, and every GarageCluster/Bucket/Key apply fails at admission — which looks like a broken CRD rather than a missing issuer.

nodes.label: Chart publishes SLSA provenance, not a cosign signature
nodes.norm_label: chart publishes slsa provenance, not a cosign signature
nodes.rationale: verify: { provider: cosign } was rejected by Flux with 'can't verify identities without providing at least one identity'. That message reads like a missing matchOIDCIdentity but is not: at this digest there is no sha256-<digest>.sig tag and the referrers index holds one artifact, a SLSA build provenance attestation (dev.sigstore.bundle, dsse-envelope). Flux's cosign provider verifies signatures and has no path to consume a SLSA attestation, so no identity regex could make it pass. Verify out-of-band with `gh attestation verify`; the digest pin is what actually protects the pull.

nodes.label: Reloader auto-restart on Connect credential rotation
nodes.norm_label: reloader auto-restart on connect credential rotation
nodes.rationale: reloader.stakater.com/auto is set on both the deployment and the service so the Connect pods restart when the sops-managed 1password-credentials.json Secret changes; the operator sub-chart is disabled (operator.create: false) because only the Connect API is wanted here.

nodes.label: github-actions namespace runs pod-security enforce=privileged
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted Actions runners need to build and run containers, so the namespace label pins pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce to privileged rather than the estate default baseline/restricted.

nodes.label: ARC controller and scale-set charts pinned in lockstep at 0.14.2
nodes.norm_label: arc controller and scale-set charts pinned in lockstep at 0.14.2
nodes.rationale: Both OCIRepositories track the same tag because the gha-runner-scale-set listener protocol is only compatible with a matching controller version; splitting the versions breaks runner registration.

nodes.label: generic-runner HelmRelease (ARC scale set base)
nodes.rationale: Single placeholder-valued gha-runner-scale-set HelmRelease acts as the shared template for every repo/org runner overlay; githubConfigUrl and githubConfigSecret are deliberately 'placeholder' so each overlay must JSON-patch them, making an unpatched overlay fail loudly rather than register against the wrong account. containerMode kubernetes with a longhorn-local RWO work PVC keeps job workspaces node-local.

nodes.label: david-driscoll-runners overlay
nodes.rationale: Registered repo-scoped against github.com/david-driscoll/crew, NOT account-scoped: david-driscoll is a User account, not an org, so a bare account URL makes ARC call /orgs/david-driscoll/... which 404s and crash-loops the listener. Personal accounts only support repo-level runners — one scale set per repo, which is why ./vault exists as a sibling instead of one shared account scale set. minRunners 0 / maxRunners 2 keeps an idle-scale-to-zero footprint.

nodes.label: littles-tech-runners overlay
nodes.rationale: Org-scoped (github.com/littlestechnology) so one scale set serves every repo in the org — the opposite of the personal-account overlays. It is the heavy tier: minRunners 1 keeps a warm runner, maxRunners 4, and it is the only overlay that add-patches container resources up to 2 CPU / 3Gi request and 8Gi limit for build-heavy jobs.

nodes.label: littles-tech-release Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: Uniquely dependsOn the sibling littles-tech Kustomization rather than gha-repositories, because it reuses the littles-tech-github-app secret that the littles-tech overlay provisions via its own ./secret.yaml — applying release first would leave the HelmRelease pointing at a missing secret.

nodes.label: littles-tech-release-runners overlay
nodes.rationale: The only overlay with no ./secret.yaml of its own — it borrows littles-tech-github-app from the sibling littles-tech overlay. Separate scale set (max 3, min 1) so release workflows get a dedicated queue that PR/CI load cannot starve.

nodes.label: vault-runners overlay
nodes.rationale: Repo-scoped against github.com/david-driscoll/vault for the same User-account-is-not-an-org reason as the david-driscoll overlay. vault is the crew's private issue tracker and the only repo whose workflows need a runner: crew-claude.yml executes here and checks out the other estate repos via an app token, so this one scale set is the entry point for all crew automation.

nodes.label: onepassword-connect HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: Tier 0 component: OpenBao cannot boot at exit without external-secrets + onepassword-connect, so both pods must remain schedulable on a control plane once the low-power tier's control-plane taint is live (docs/cluster-consolidation/20-low-power-tier.md §4). connect.tolerations and operator.tolerations are SEPARATE chart keys — setting only one silently leaves the other pod untolerated, so both are set. Reloader annotations on the deployment and service force a restart when the credentials secret or access token rotates.

nodes.label: onepassword-connect HTTPRoute (disabled)
nodes.rationale: A Gateway API HTTPRoute onto the network/internal Gateway that would expose op-connect.${CLUSTER_DOMAIN} to port 8080, but it is commented out of kustomization.yaml — the chart's own Traefik ingress (ingressClassName internal) currently owns that hostname instead. Kept in-tree as the migration target rather than deleted.

nodes.label: onepassword-connect Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: Supplies APP and NAMESPACE via postBuild.substitute, which is what lets uptime.yaml name itself ${APP} and stay generic. wait: true because downstream ExternalSecret stores cannot reconcile until Connect is actually serving.

nodes.label: 1Password Connect ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: Custom driscoll.dev/v1 ApplicationDefinition CR that declares the Gatus health probe (https://op-connect.${CLUSTER_DOMAIN}/health expecting 200) and the admins-only access policy in one place, so monitoring and authz are derived from the app manifest rather than hand-maintained in a central Gatus config.

nodes.label: Cilium Hubble ApplicationDefinition (commented out)
nodes.rationale: Entirely commented out, yet still listed in kustomization.yaml resources — it renders to nothing today. It preserves the intended shape of Hubble exposure: an Authentik forward_single proxy in front of hubble.${CLUSTER_DOMAIN} with an admins-only policy and a matching Gatus check, ready to re-enable.

nodes.label: cilium HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: Carries no inline values at all: everything comes from valuesFrom the cilium-values ConfigMap, which the sibling kustomization.yaml generates from ./helm/values.yaml. That indirection keeps the CNI config a plain YAML file (editable/lintable) while still getting Kustomize's hash-suffixed ConfigMap regeneration on change.

nodes.label: cilium HelmRepository
nodes.rationale: Deliberately declared in kube-system rather than flux-system — the inline comment states the namespace is required for Renovate lookups to resolve the chart version.

nodes.label: cilium Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: deletionPolicy: Orphan so the CNI is never cascade-deleted merely because ownership of the Kustomization changes (e.g. a namespace-redirect flip during consolidation) — see docs/cluster-consolidation/27-migration-churn-failure-modes.md. wait: false because Cilium's own readiness would deadlock a health check that depends on cluster networking already working.

nodes.label: cilium Kustomization (values ConfigMap generator)
nodes.rationale: configMapGenerator turns ./helm/values.yaml into the cilium-values ConfigMap, and ./helm/kustomizeconfig.yaml teaches Kustomize to rewrite the hashed name into the HelmRelease's valuesFrom reference — without that configurations entry the HelmRelease would point at a stale, non-existent ConfigMap name.

nodes.label: CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy l2-policy
nodes.rationale: ARP-announces the pool's LoadBalancer IPs on Linux nodes. The interface regexes (ens*, enp*s*, eth*) exist because a host with more than one active NIC would otherwise announce on the wrong link; this is the L2 (no BGP) path to service reachability.

nodes.label: CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool pool
nodes.rationale: Two blocks (.100-.200 and .202-.252) inside ${LOADBALANCER_RANGE} with a deliberate gap at .201, reserving that address for something outside Cilium's allocator. allowFirstLastIPs: No keeps network/broadcast addresses out of the pool.

nodes.label: gha-arc-controller (ARC controller dependency)
nodes.rationale: Every runner scale set both dependsOn the controller HelmRelease and names its service account (gha-arc-controller/github-actions) in values.controllerServiceAccount, so the controller is a hard ordering and RBAC prerequisite for all four overlays.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition (driscoll.dev/v1) convention
nodes.rationale: Estate-local CRD (schema at schemas/definition.schema.json) that colocates dashboard icon/category, Authentik access policy, and Gatus checks with the app that owns them. Instances template on ${APP}, ${CLUSTER_TITLE} and ${CLUSTER_DOMAIN} so the same file works per-cluster.

nodes.label: Repo-scoped ARC registration for personal accounts
nodes.norm_label: repo-scoped arc registration for personal accounts
nodes.rationale: GitHub User accounts have no /orgs/<name> endpoint, so ARC's listener 404s and crash-loops if given a bare account githubConfigUrl. The estate therefore pays a one-scale-set-per-repo cost for david-driscoll/crew and david-driscoll/vault, while littlestechnology (a real org) gets a single account-scoped scale set covering all its repos.

nodes.label: tailnet-inbound ProxyGroup

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: meilisearch-env
nodes.rationale: Pulls the master key from OpenBao path clusters/equestria/apps/meilisearch/secret-key (was the 1Password item 'MeiliSearch Secret Key') and rewrites every field to a meili_ prefix so the template can address it as .meili_password.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: meilisearch
nodes.rationale: Broken out of karakeep into a standalone release so the search engine can be versioned and upgraded independently. Uses the upstream meilisearch chart (0.38.0) rather than app-template because the chart owns the StatefulSet, persistence and serviceMonitor wiring.

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: n8n-env
nodes.rationale: Composes two stores into one env Secret: app credentials (encryption key, license key) from the OpenBao ClusterSecretStore at clusters/equestria/apps/n8n/credentials, and rotating Postgres connection fields from the `database` ClusterSecretStore item ${APP}-postgres. Carries cnpg.io/reload and reloader annotations so a rotation restarts the pod.

nodes.label: ConfigMap generator: n8n-hooks
nodes.rationale: Generated from resources/hooks.js with disableNameSuffixHash and kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/substitute: disabled, so Flux post-build substitution never rewrites JavaScript that legitimately contains ${...} and the mount path stays stable.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: obsidian-sync (CouchDB)
nodes.rationale: Plain couchdb image under app-template running as uid/gid 5984 with a matching fsGroup so the Longhorn volume at /opt/couchdb/data is writable. A cors.ini ConfigMap is mounted into local.d because Obsidian LiveSync clients are browser/Electron origins; the in-container CORS config is permissive and the real origin allow-list is enforced at the Traefik edge.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: obsidian-sync
nodes.rationale: VOLSYNC_PUID/PGID are pinned to 5984 to match the CouchDB user, so restic restores land with ownership the container can use.

nodes.label: Traefik Middleware: obsidian-sync-cors
nodes.rationale: Edge-enforced CORS allow-list for the Obsidian client surfaces: https://app.obsidian.md (web), app://obsidian.md (desktop), capacitor://localhost and http://localhost (mobile). Headers are enumerated explicitly rather than wildcarded so credentialed requests stay valid.

nodes.label: Job: obsidian-sync-init (CouchDB bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: post-install Helm hook that polls http://obsidian-sync:5984/_up until ready, then PUTs the three system databases (_users, _replicator, _global_changes) that CouchDB will not create for itself. Credentials come from env vars rather than the URL so they never appear in the process list; each PUT is `|| true` so a re-run on an already-initialised cluster is idempotent.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Outline
nodes.rationale: Declares a confidential Authentik OAuth2 client with redirect URIs for both the public and the tailnet hostname, and subMode user_email so Outline identifies accounts by email — real OIDC rather than the forward-auth proxy mode the other apps in this directory use.

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: outline-values
nodes.rationale: Three-store fan-in (onepassword-connect for the app secret key, `database` for Postgres, `cluster` for the Authentik OIDC client) rendered through templateFrom against the ${APP}-values ConfigMap, producing a complete values.yaml as Secret data. This is the mechanism that lets the HelmRelease keep zero inline values. Unlike the other apps in this directory it still reads from 1Password rather than OpenBao.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: outline
nodes.rationale: Community chart release whose entire values document is supplied by valuesFrom a Secret (${APP}-values) instead of inline values, so the OIDC client secret and Postgres password never appear in git.

nodes.label: MEILI_ENV production auth enforcement
nodes.rationale: Meilisearch was pinned to MEILI_ENV=development only because the master key rendered empty and production refuses to boot on a key under 16 bytes. Now that meilisearch-env resolves a real 42-byte key from OpenBao, flipping to production makes the server ENFORCE auth. The StatefulSet carries no reloader annotation, so the Secret gaining a value never restarted the pod; editing the chart's `environment:` map changes its config checksum annotation, which rolls the pod and picks up key and setting together. Also carries MEILI_UPGRADE_DB=true for the one-way on-startup 1.47.0 -> 1.51.0 DB migration. The chart key is `environment:` (rendered into a ConfigMap consumed via envFrom), NOT `env:` — an earlier `env:` block was silently ignored (vault#102).

nodes.label: Phase 6 pilot: first ExternalSecret moved to OpenBao
nodes.norm_label: phase 6 pilot: first externalsecret moved to openbao
nodes.rationale: Chosen deliberately as the first 1Password -> OpenBao cutover: one standalone app, one key, nothing else depends on the Secret, and a failure surfaces as CouchDB rejecting auth rather than as anything cluster-wide. The key is a path inside the `secrets` mount (the store pins path: secrets, so it is not repeated), and Phase 4 migrated the item field-for-field so the `username`/`password` field names — and therefore the template — needed no edit.

nodes.label: Dropped-app parking and the postgres re-enable trap
nodes.norm_label: dropped-app parking and the postgres re-enable trap
nodes.rationale: Outline was dropped (group E, 2026-08-25) and the whole ks.yaml is parked — the parent kustomization has it commented out too, which is why the file is commented rather than deleted. The components/postgres line specifically must NOT be uncommented as a restore step: the Database CR, the database and the login role were all removed, and the Pulumi `system` stack discovers that component and creates database/static-roles/${APP}, which fails outright until CNPG has recreated the role. See the ORDER OF OPERATIONS block in components/postgres/ks.yaml.

nodes.label: GrafanaDashboard: Pecron Batteries

nodes.label: Hermes config deep-merge semantics
nodes.community_name: Dashboard auth gate fails closed on non-loopback bind
nodes.rationale: hermes_cli/config.py::_load_config_impl deep-copies DEFAULT_CONFIG and _deep_merges the user file over it on every read, with no reference to the schema version. Dict sections merge key-by-key but a list REPLACES the default outright — which is exactly the behaviour the narrowed platform_toolsets.cli list depends on, and why a partial config is safe.

nodes.label: _config_version: 33
nodes.community_name: Dashboard auth gate fails closed on non-loopback bind
nodes.rationale: Without the key the container logged '[config-migrate] WARNING: This config predates version 12 (~2 years old)' on every boot. Two upstream paths disagree: hermes_cli/config.py::migrate_config calls _raw_config_has_explicit_version() and treats a missing key as a fresh minimal config (so the CLI would migrate and stamp normally), but scripts/docker_config_migrate.py — what actually runs at boot — coerces a missing key to 0 via check_config_version(), takes the below-floor branch, prints the warning and returns 0 without ever calling migrate_config. Crucially the file was NOT discarded: the below-floor branch is warn-and-continue, config_migrations.py documents the file as left byte-for-byte untouched, load_config() has no version gate, and tools_config.py::_get_platform_tools reads platform_toolsets off the merged config — containment was in force the whole time. 33 is DEFAULT_CONFIG['_config_version'] in hermes_cli/config_defaults.py at the pinned tag, so docker_config_migrate.py short-circuits at current_ver >= latest_ver and never runs a migration pass that would strip every comment. When Renovate bumps the image and raises the latest version, the boot migrator rewrites the LIVE config (comments included) — normal, but bump this number when re-seeding a rebuilt host.

nodes.label: Narrowed platform_toolsets.cli
nodes.community_name: Dashboard auth gate fails closed on non-loopback bind
nodes.rationale: Kept: web, terminal, file, skills, todo, memory, session_search, clarify — enough to be useful while the shell stays the only high-power verb, contained by the container boundary. Removed with reasons: code_execution spawns a HOST subprocess from the agent's own interpreter, bypassing terminal-backend isolation, and terminal already covers running things with better guards; cronjob lets the agent schedule its own recurring work, a persistence mechanism matching the shape of the June 2026 MCP-config persistence campaign; delegation spawns sub-agents, multiplying spend and obscuring the audit trail; browser needs BROWSERBASE_API_KEY (external cloud browser with residential proxies and CAPTCHA solving) and is inert without it, listed so 'off' is a decision not an accident; computer_use has no display; vision/image_gen/tts/stt need provider keys not set. UNVERIFIED caveat: bfl reports enabled even when omitted, apparently registering outside platform_toolsets — inert without an API key but worth investigating if the toolset list ever seems not to apply.

nodes.label: terminal.backend: local (whole-process wrapping)
nodes.community_name: Dashboard auth gate fails closed on non-loopback bind
nodes.rationale: 'local' runs tool commands inside this container as the unprivileged hermes user. Upstream calls this whole-process wrapping (SECURITY.md 2.2) and it is the supported way to contain everything — shell, code execution, MCP subprocesses, plugins, hooks, skill loading. The alternative, terminal-backend isolation, only confines what goes through the shell and would additionally require handing this container a docker socket. cwd is pinned to /opt/data/workspace so tool commands do not start next to sessions/, memories/ and .env.

nodes.label: GOMEMLIMIT and Container Limit Must Move Together
nodes.norm_label: gomemlimit and container limit must move together
nodes.rationale: The chart's 128Mi/GOMEMLIMIT=110MiB OOMKilled this operator 23 times in a row. GOMEMLIMIT is a soft ceiling on the Go HEAP only — it does not cover goroutine stacks, runtime overhead, or above all the informer caches, which is where the memory goes because rbac.scope: cluster makes every one of ~20 controllers cache its kind across ALL namespaces. Raising only the container limit leaves Go targeting a 110MiB heap and collecting too aggressively; raising only GOMEMLIMIT walks back into the OOM.

nodes.label: rbac.scope cluster and Its Bargain
nodes.rationale: The ClusterRole carries create/update/delete on Deployments, StatefulSets, Services, Secrets, ConfigMaps, ServiceAccounts, Roles and RoleBindings bound cluster-wide, so 'may create an MCPServer in namespace X' is effectively 'may run a pod, and mint RBAC for it, in namespace X'. Same bargain as CNPG, Garage and external-secrets, and it holds for the same reason: writing an MCPServer means writing to this Git repo. allowedNamespaces is NOT the lever to narrow it — that only applies under scope: namespace, and switching costs the StorageVersionMigrator.

nodes.label: storageVersionMigrator Feature
nodes.rationale: Only possible because scope is cluster — the chart's validate-features.yaml fails the render outright for any other combination, since this controller watches cluster-scoped CRDs and re-stores objects across every namespace. It keeps status.storedVersions trimmed to what is live, so a future release dropping a deprecated API version cannot orphan objects still stored under the old one. Without it that cleanup is manual, must happen BEFORE such a release lands, and nothing in-cluster warns you.

nodes.label: Per-Value remoteRef Instead of dataFrom.extract
nodes.rationale: The nineteen-field shared/media-management-secrets blob was split (docs/openbao-shared-secrets-reorg.md §G) and Kometa wanted seven of them. Explicit data: entries remove the EMPTY-IS-NOT-MISSING hazard of dataFrom.extract: a template referencing an absent field failed the whole ExternalSecret under missingkey=error, whereas a data: entry naming a nonexistent path fails naming the path, not the template variable. tmdb_apikey was dropped from the blob rather than moved because it duplicated third-party-tokens/tmdb/api-key that xcproxy already reads — two homes for one vendor key means no way to tell which one a rotation updated.

nodes.label: Two-Step Secret Key Rewrite
nodes.rationale: The first regexp normalises the credential Secret's hyphenated keys (public-hostname, jdbc-uri, connection-string) into legal Go template identifiers; the second prefixes postgres_. Only five plain keys are used, but normalising all of them means adding a sixth needs no thought. The keys are spelled out rather than dataFrom-ed through because Lidarr reads LIDARR__SECTION__KEY env vars whose prefix is not derivable from ${APP} — kustomize has no upper-case function.

nodes.label: PostgresHost as the Postgres On-Switch
nodes.rationale: Sonarr-family apps use Postgres if and only if PostgresHost is non-empty (NzbDrone.Core/Datastore/ConnectionStringFactory.cs). Deleting this ExternalSecret and the envFrom that reads it drops the app back onto the SQLite file still sitting in its config PVC — that is the rollback, and why the file is not deleted.

nodes.label: Servarr main/log Database Pair
nodes.rationale: Lidarr opens both ${APP} and ${APP}-log at startup and creates neither, so the log database must exist first (declared in ./postgres-databases/, rendered by components/postgres/databases). The main DB is renamed from the wiki's <app>-main because components/postgres names an app's database after the app; -log keeps the wiki name because nothing constrains it. Both share ONE credential — ConnectionStringFactory varies only the database name — so there is no second role and no second OpenBao static role. LOGDB is therefore a literal, not a Secret key.

nodes.rationale: The 14 toolhive.stacklok.dev CRDs, split from the operator the way upstream ships them. The split is not cosmetic: it lets the operator be uninstalled, rolled back or re-scoped without reaching the MCPServer objects. rollback.force is FALSE unlike most releases here — a forced rollback deletes and recreates what it cannot patch, and deleting a CRD takes every MCPServer with it. crds.keep stamps helm.sh/resource-policy: keep, which is the only thing standing between an uninstall and a cascade delete since this chart renders CRDs from templates/ rather than crds/.

nodes.rationale: Helm stores each retained revision as one Secret holding the gzipped chart AND the rendered manifest — ~450 KB per revision here against Kubernetes' 1 MB Secret ceiling. History is not the risk (three revisions is three separate Secrets); upstream growing the definitions is. A 'request entity too large' error on a sh.helm.release.v1.* Secret is this, not a cluster problem.

nodes.label: toolhive-operator HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: The chart renders SIX objects and none is a Service, Ingress or HTTPRoute — everything with an HTTP surface in this namespace is created by the operator at runtime from a CR, which is why the route and the authorization server live in ../toolhive. No image/toolhiveRunnerImage/vmcpImage overrides on purpose, so the OCIRepository tag is the single version to bump and the operator can never drift from the proxy-runner image it injects. No priorityClassName and no control-plane toleration: MCP servers are developer tooling, so during a Low Power window the operator and its proxy runners go Pending together, which is the correct outcome.

nodes.label: toolhive-operator PodMonitor
nodes.rationale: A PodMonitor rather than a ServiceMonitor because the chart renders NO Service at all. The selector matches the chart's own selectorLabels, not this Kustomization's commonMetadata — commonMetadata lands on the HelmRelease, never on the pods Helm renders from it, and app.kubernetes.io/instance is the RELEASE name, which is why fullnameOverride is restated. The operator takes no --metrics-secure flag, so this is a plain scrape with no TLS and no bearer token.

nodes.norm_label: gatus core config (storage, alerting, ui, web)
nodes.rationale: SQLite at /data/data.db with caching, concurrency 2, web port 9595. Defines the pushover default-alert every endpoint file inherits.

nodes.label: Gatus external-endpoint: Forgejo Actions canary
nodes.rationale: 3h heartbeat tolerating two missed runs of an hourly (17 * * * *) scheduled workflow — enough to ride out a node move, a Low Power window or a cold image pull, short enough to catch a wedged runner the same morning.

nodes.label: Gatus external-endpoint: openbao nightly-dump
nodes.rationale: Nightly at 03:00; 26h heartbeat interval so one missed dump goes red.

nodes.label: Gatus external-endpoint: openbao restore-test
nodes.rationale: Monthly on the 1st at 05:00; 792h (33 day) heartbeat covers a 31-day month plus one retry window. Past that the backup is formally untrusted per RUNBOOK Scenario D and someone should hear about it daily.

nodes.label: zwave-js-ui container
nodes.rationale: Binds the Silicon Labs HubZ USB controller via a stable /dev/serial/by-id path mapped to /dev/zwave, so the device survives re-enumeration. tty + stop_signal SIGINT for clean shutdown; ports 8091 (UI) and 3000 (Z-Wave JS websocket for Home Assistant) published on the host.

nodes.label: instance/hostname relabel pattern
nodes.rationale: Shared relabel recipe: copy __address__ into instance, then strip the :port with regex ([^:]+).* into a hostname label. Used identically by every host-specific scrape file so dashboards can group by hostname.

nodes.label: Gatus merged-directory config model
nodes.rationale: GATUS_CONFIG_PATH points at a directory; every YAML inside is merged into a single effective config. This is what lets Pulumi-generated endpoints and hand-written in-repo endpoint files coexist without either owning the whole file.

nodes.label: Pushover alerting provider
nodes.rationale: Credentials come from OpenBao via vals-style ref+openbao:// references to secrets/third-party-tokens/pushover/gatus. failure-threshold 4 / success-threshold 2 by default; individual heartbeat endpoints override to 1/1 because a lapsed heartbeat is already a multi-hour signal.

nodes.label: toGatusKey(group, name) token convention
nodes.rationale: External-endpoint push tokens are derived from group and name by toGatusKey in home-operations/components/helpers.ts (e.g. openbao-break-glass_nightly-dump, forgejo-actions_canary). Hand-written endpoint files must follow the same derivation so they are indistinguishable from the Pulumi-generated ones and reporters can compute the token.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition CRD (driscoll.dev/v1)
nodes.rationale: Repo-local schema (schemas/definition.schema.json) describing each Dockge stack to the estate tooling: display name, category, icon, access_policy groups, optional authentik oauth2 client, and gatus endpoint definitions. It is the single declaration that drives SSO client creation and uptime checks for a docker stack.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Uptime
nodes.rationale: Infrastructure category, access_policy groups friends+family, self-monitoring gatus check on its own URL.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Z-Wave
nodes.rationale: admins-only access policy; simple 200 gatus check on the websecure hostname.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: llama.cpp Agent Server
nodes.rationale: Category AI, no access_policy or authentik block. Probed through Traefik rather than ${ipAddress}:8081 so the check covers the route Hermes' operators actually click; because the container port stays published, a failure here means 'hostname is broken' not 'llama.cpp is down'. /health only returns 200 once the model is fully loaded.

nodes.label: Dropped gatus scrape job
nodes.rationale: The gatus job was deleted rather than migrated: it targeted gatus:8080 but the container is named uptime and listens on 9595, and Gatus only serves /metrics when metrics: true is set (it is not). Reviving it would have added a permanently-down target; enabling Gatus metrics is a separate piece of work.

nodes.label: scrape_config_files glob loading
nodes.rationale: Host-specific scrape jobs are loaded via the scrape_config_files glob in docker/_common/prometheus/config/prometheus.yml. A file merely copied into the container is silently ignored unless the glob picks it up — the failure mode is a config that looks correct and does nothing.

nodes.label: Gatus /config mount must not be :ro
nodes.rationale: Gatus merges every YAML in GATUS_CONFIG_PATH into one config, so Pulumi-written endpoint files and in-repo static files must share a directory, the static ones layered as individual file mounts. runc has to CREATE a mountpoint inside the parent for any layered file that does not already exist, and on a :ro parent that create fails with 'make mountpoint: read-only file system' before the container process starts. default.yaml only escaped it via a stale 0-byte twin from June; openbao-break-glass.yaml had no twin and took the whole uptime stack down. The individual file mounts stay :ro — that is where read-only belongs.

nodes.label: Dead-man's switch for CI liveness
nodes.rationale: The Forgejo Actions runner is only observable WHILE FAILING: the ForgejoRunnerDown and ForgejoRunnerFlapping PrometheusRules watch the pod, and Forgejo exports no runner metric at all (modules/metrics/collector.go, gitea_ namespace, 28 series, none about runners). A pod that is Running, Ready, registered and no longer accepting jobs is indistinguishable from an idle CI system — a revoked registration, a wedged poller and an expired token all look identical. Only a job that is SUPPOSED to run separates idle from broken. Bonus coverage: the canary lives inside Forgejo as a repo+workflow, so anything that destroys Forgejo's data volume destroys it and the silence alerts — the 2026-08-24 volume loss passed unnoticed for exactly this reason.

nodes.label: Heartbeat silence as an enforceable failure
nodes.norm_label: heartbeat silence as an enforceable failure
nodes.rationale: The openbao-replica cronjobs POST success/failure through the dockge-as egress. Two loud failure modes: success=false turns the endpoint red immediately, and reporting nothing at all lapses the heartbeat interval and turns it red anyway. Silence is the dangerous one — RUNBOOK Scenario D declares a backup that has not proven itself in over a month UNTRUSTED, and these heartbeats are what make that statement enforceable rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: In-cluster sops-age Secret rotation
nodes.rationale: kustomize-controller decrypts with a mounted identity from kubernetes/flux/meta/sops-age.sops.yaml applied via scripts/bootstrap-apps.sh; after the sweep it must be re-applied on both clusters and trimmed to the surviving identity, otherwise Flux keeps a retired key alive.

nodes.label: Forgejo Actions Canary Workflow
nodes.rationale: Proves the Actions runner is not merely Running but actually executing jobs, by pushing hourly into a Gatus external endpoint whose heartbeat fails if no push arrives. This file is the canonical copy; the one that executes lives inside Forgejo, which is manual state. Forgejo only schedules workflows on the repository's DEFAULT branch. A heartbeat that hangs is a heartbeat that pages, hence timeout-minutes: 5.

nodes.label: gitssh Gateway Listener on Port 22
nodes.rationale: The container still binds 2222 because the rootless image runs as uid 1000; only the Service, listener and advertised port are 22. Talos nodes run no sshd and this binds the Gateway LoadBalancer IP, so nothing collides. The tailnet grant forgejo-git-ssh is restricted to tag:apps and must never be folded back into default-apps-access, which also reaches tag:dockge and tag:dns where 22 is a real shell.
nodes.source_location: What the manifests already do — SSH

nodes.label: Offline Forgejo Actions Runner Registration
nodes.rationale: Offline registration so the credential is one we chose rather than pasted from the UI. The printed UUID is not random — it is the hex encoding of the token's first 16 characters, so re-running with the same first 16 and different last 24 ROTATES the secret in place instead of creating a second runner. replicas must stay 1: every replica would read the same registration secret and share one runner identity.

nodes.label: stacks/system Forgejo Bot Provisioning
nodes.rationale: Two grant mechanisms because Forgejo has two kinds of owner: an org `renovate` team with includesAllRepositories covers future repositories automatically, while user-owned repositories need one collaborator grant each and so lag by a stack run. Archived, mirror and fork repositories are skipped deliberately. The stack authenticates as the BREAK-GLASS ADMIN with username and password, not a token, because Forgejo's /users/{username}/tokens route is reqBasicOrRevProxyAuth — a token-authenticated request cannot mint a token at all. Rotating that admin password is a Forgejo operation followed by a bao kv put, in that order.

nodes.label: GITHUB_COM_TOKEN from the Reflected GitHub App Token
nodes.norm_label: github_com_token from the reflected github app token
nodes.rationale: Renovate needs one — unauthenticated api.github.com is 60 requests an hour for the whole egress IP — but it already exists: the GitHub App installation token stacks/vault/KubernetesGithubAppToken.ts mints and emberstack reflects. It expires hourly and is re-minted, harmless because every Renovate pod is a short-lived Job. The driscoll.dev/token-expires-at annotation is the only non-secret evidence the value underneath is current.
nodes.source_location: There is no github.com credential to create

nodes.label: renovate-operator Policy Engine
nodes.rationale: Turned on though the chart ships it off. Bounds every URL taken from a RenovateJob: allowedHosts, allowedImages, and requireSecretRefOptIn (a Secret must label itself allow-ref: true). A policy denial leaves the job silently idle with Accepted: False — the condition's reason names the value to fix. Combined with rbac.ownNamespaceOnly so a RenovateJob elsewhere cannot borrow its credentials.
nodes.source_location: What the manifests already do — The policy engine

nodes.label: Forgejo celestia to equestria Cutover
nodes.rationale: A re-create, not a migration — the celestia instance holds no repositories. Lands in the existing `coder` namespace rather than a new one because that is already the Low Power keep-list namespace and already carries the local-user middleware and the app-template OCIRepository.

nodes.label: Renovate for Forgejo
nodes.rationale: Three pieces: the mogenius renovate-operator, one RenovateJob CR, and stacks/system/forgejo-renovate.ts which creates the bot account and mints its token. Split into two Kubernetes apps for the same reason garage-system splits cluster from operator — the second contains nothing but a custom resource whose CRD ships with the first's chart. Does not touch the GitHub side.

nodes.label: curl --connect-to Tailnet Egress Hop
nodes.rationale: Pods have no direct route to the tailnet, so --connect-to keeps Host and SNI intact (Traefik still routes, the Let's Encrypt certificate still validates) while the connection actually goes out through the dockge-as egress. GATUS_TOKEN is both the URL path segment and the bearer — that is Gatus's external-endpoint convention.

nodes.label: Pulumi vs external-dns Race on git.driscoll.tech
nodes.norm_label: pulumi vs external-dns race on git.driscoll.tech
nodes.rationale: stacks/home deletes the old celestia CNAME (DockgeLxc reads traefik router rule labels out of compose files) while external-dns tries to claim the same name under policy: sync with a txtOwnerId, so it will not adopt a record it does not own. It self-heals on retry; the trap is the window during which git.driscoll.tech still resolves to celestia where the OLD Forgejo is still running — it is entirely possible to log into the old instance and conclude the new one is broken.
nodes.source_location: 2. Merge, and watch two Pulumi stacks race external-dns

nodes.label: Deleting a Dockge Stack Directory Does Not Stop the Container
nodes.norm_label: deleting a dockge stack directory does not stop the container
nodes.rationale: Dockge's .ignore path removes /opt/stacks/<stack>/ and leaves the container running and orphaned, and restart: unless-stopped plus autoheal resurrect it indefinitely. Requires a manual `docker rm -f`. The old database is likewise orphaned because provision.sh only ever creates, never reaps.

nodes.label: Dedicated Single-Node Garage for Forgejo Objects
nodes.norm_label: dedicated single-node garage for forgejo objects
nodes.rationale: One [storage] STORAGE_TYPE = minio block backs all eight object subsystems. replication.factor: 1 because 3x replication in front of an app that cannot run two replicas is redundancy that can never be exercised; durability comes from longhorn-critical underneath. Bare git repositories are NOT among the eight — Forgejo always keeps those on disk, so the PVC is still what a restore rebuilds the forge from. Its RPC secret must never be shared with garage-system or a node from one cluster could join the other's mesh.
nodes.source_location: What the manifests already do — Object storage

nodes.label: Forgejo JWT_SECRET Length Failure Is Silent
nodes.norm_label: forgejo jwt_secret length failure is silent
nodes.rationale: [security] SECRET_KEY is free-form but [oauth2] JWT_SECRET must decode to exactly 32 bytes. Given 48, Forgejo logs one line and proceeds with a key it invented — and because the chart rebuilds app.ini from the environment on every boot, that key differs every restart, so Actions task tokens and OAuth2 tokens silently die with the pod. Verify with `logs -c configure-gitea | grep -i jwt_secret`; silence is success.

nodes.label: Pulumi-Written OIDC Credential Bootstrap Cycle
nodes.rationale: The pod crash-loops until pulumi/equestria (stacks/applications) resyncs, reads the ApplicationDefinition CR out of the live cluster, creates the authentik application and provider, and writes clusters/equestria/apps/forgejo/oidc. ESO picks it up within its 4m refresh — allow ~10 minutes end to end. This circularity is the mechanism, not a fault.

nodes.label: Runner Canary Bootstrap (manual state)
nodes.rationale: Forgejo exports no runner metric at all, so a runner that is up but no longer accepting jobs — revoked registration, wedged poller — looks healthy to both ForgejoRunnerDown and ForgejoRunnerFlapping. Only a job that is SUPPOSED to run can tell 'nobody pushed today' from 'the poller is wedged'. It covers its own disappearance: whatever destroys the data volume destroys the canary repo, so the heartbeat lapses. It is manual state — a VolSync restore brings it back only if the repository was in the snapshot.

nodes.label: Second Garage Bucket for Renovate Logs and Cache
nodes.norm_label: second garage bucket for renovate logs and cache
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a second bucket on the Forgejo Garage cluster, not a prefix in `forgejo` — that one is backed up nightly and everything here is rebuildable. Size tracks repository count, not run count, because both prefixes are keyed by identity and each run overwrites the last. The log store fails QUIETLY: a log-store failure does not fail the Renovate run it was recording.
nodes.source_location: Log storage and the repository cache

nodes.label: gitUrl endpoint — Clone Host Must Match Auth Host
nodes.norm_label: giturl endpoint — clone host must match auth host
nodes.rationale: Renovate keys its git credential to the host of `endpoint` (the in-cluster Service), but Forgejo advertises a public clone_url, so the two hosts differ and no credential matches. Discovery never notices because it only calls the API and never clones.
nodes.source_location: Troubleshooting — The executor fails on every repository

nodes.label: local> Presets Break on a Second Platform
nodes.norm_label: local> presets break on a second platform
nodes.rationale: local> resolves against whatever platform the bot is on, so on the Forgejo bot it looks for the repo on git.driscoll.tech instead of GitHub. .github/renovate.json5 therefore names its shared preset as github>david-driscoll/.github:renovate-config — identical on GitHub, and the only spelling that survives being consumed from a second platform. A new local> anywhere in the chain breaks Forgejo and nothing on GitHub.
nodes.source_location: Troubleshooting — Every repository errors with preset not found

nodes.label: Bridged Terraform Provider Version Lives in a base64 Blob
nodes.norm_label: bridged terraform provider version lives in a base64 blob
nodes.rationale: A Renovate bump is half a change and the missing half is silent: sdks/forgejo/package.json restates the version inside a base64 pulumi.parameterization.value, which is what the bridge actually resolves from. No regex can re-encode it, so a merged bump that was not regenerated reads 1.6.0 -> 1.7.0 while pulumi up keeps running 1.6.0 with no error. Also: `pulumi package add` rewrites its Pulumi.yaml entry as a BLOCK sequence while the Renovate customManager matches the flow form, so left as a block the provider silently stops being tracked.
nodes.source_location: Keeping the Terraform provider up to date

nodes.label: Forgejo ALLOWED_HOST_LIST for ClusterIP Webhook Delivery
nodes.norm_label: forgejo allowed_host_list for clusterip webhook delivery
nodes.rationale: Forgejo's default is `external` — valid non-private unicast IPs only — so without this every delivery to the operator's ClusterIP is dropped BEFORE it leaves the Forgejo pod, visible only in Forgejo's own delivery history. It names the exact host rather than the built-in `private` group on purpose: `private` would re-open delivery to every RFC1918 address, turning any repository's webhook settings into an SSRF primitive against the estate.
