nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: OpenBooks
nodes.rationale: driscoll.dev/v1 ApplicationDefinition is the estate's single declaration point for an app's identity: it drives the Authentik forward_single proxy provider, the media-managers access policy, and the Gatus HTTP check, so those three concerns never drift apart per-app.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: openbooks
nodes.rationale: IRC book-fetch daemon (evanbuss/openbooks) run with --persist and --no-browser-downloads so downloads land on the shared truenas-media claim under downloads/openbooks instead of being streamed to a browser.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: openbooks
nodes.rationale: Pulls in the shared tailscale and volsync components and substitutes APP/NAMESPACE, so the HelmRelease can template ${APP}.${ROOT_DOMAIN} without repeating the app name.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: bookbounty-audio
nodes.rationale: Sidecar acquisition helper for the audio Readarr instance; sync_schedule is 12 (offset from the ebook instance's 0) so the two BookBounty instances never hit libgen or Readarr at the same hour.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Readarr Audio
nodes.rationale: Restricted to the media-managers group, unlike the ebook instance which is opened to family and friends — the audio instance is an operator tool, not a patron-facing library.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: readarr-audio
nodes.rationale: Second Readarr instance (INSTANCENAME 'Readarr (Audio)') sharing the same image, port 8787, API key secret and truenas-media mounts as the ebook instance; only the config PVC (readarr-audio-config) is distinct, which is what keeps the two libraries separate.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: readarr-audio
nodes.rationale: dependsOn the readarr Kustomization because the shared readarr-apikey Secret is only rendered by the readarr-ebook directory; ordering the audio instance behind it avoids a start with a missing secretKeyRef.

nodes.label: Secret: readarr-apikey (SOPS/age)
nodes.rationale: One age-encrypted API key shared by BOTH Readarr instances and BOTH BookBounty helpers, so a rotation is a single-file change; it is the only SOPS secret in the books tree (everything else moved to ExternalSecrets).

nodes.label: HelmRelease: bookbounty
nodes.rationale: Ebook-side acquisition helper; both BookBounty instances write into the SAME truenas-media subPath downloads/bookbounty, so the on-disk staging area is shared even though the config PVCs are not.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Readarr Ebook
nodes.rationale: access_policy grants family and friends (not media-managers), marking the ebook instance as the patron-facing one of the pair.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: readarr
nodes.rationale: Primary Readarr; READARR__AUTH__METHOD External with REQUIRED DisabledForLocalAddresses defers authentication to the Authentik forward-auth middleware on the HTTPRoute while leaving in-cluster API calls (BookBounty) unauthenticated apart from the API key.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: readarr
nodes.rationale: Named 'readarr' (not 'readarr-ebook') even though its path is books/readarr-ebook — the audio instance's dependsOn refers to this name, so the directory/name mismatch is load-bearing.

nodes.label: busybox chown/chmod restore initContainer
nodes.rationale: Repeated verbatim in openbooks, readarr, readarr-audio and both bookbounty releases: a root initContainer named 'restore' chowns the config path to 568:568 before the non-root app starts. It exists because volsync restores land with the mover's ownership, so without it a restored PVC would be unwritable by uid 568.

nodes.label: local-user Traefik middleware filter
nodes.rationale: Every books HTTPRoute attaches the same ExtensionRef filter (traefik.io Middleware 'local-user') in the network namespace. This is the estate's uniform 'authenticate at the edge, trust in-cluster' boundary; the app containers themselves run with External auth and no built-in login.

nodes.label: GrafanaFolder: K8S
nodes.rationale: k8s.yaml is NOT listed in the dashboards kustomization.yaml resources, so this folder and its six dashboards are not actually rendered by Flux -- either dead config or an accidental omission alongside kubernetes.yaml, which covers the same dotdc dashboards by grafana.com id.

nodes.label: GrafanaFolder: Kubernetes
nodes.rationale: The folder that is actually deployed: kubernetes.yaml is in the dashboards kustomization resources list, k8s.yaml is not.

nodes.label: pgloader Data-Only Load Job
nodes.rationale: Everything unusual is there because the alternative goes wrong: quote identifiers (or pgloader folds to lower case and finds no "Movies"), data only (or it builds its own schema over the app's), backoffLimit: 0 (a partially loaded database must never be loaded into twice), a digest-pinned amd64-only image, $(PGLOADER_TARGET) expanded by the kubelet not a shell, and the RWO config PVC attachable only because the app is scaled to zero. The target URI's password must be percent-encoded or a /, @, : or # produces a URI that parses wrong without complaining.

nodes.label: autobrrctl db:convert First-Party Converter
nodes.rationale: Runs the Postgres migration chain itself, so the target must be an EMPTY database — skip the schema-init and truncate steps. Foreign-key violations are dropped and reported rather than fatal, and are usually pre-existing orphans because SQLite does not enforce foreign keys by default. Everyone is logged out once (session store follows the driver and the converter skips the sessions table) and autobrr's own SQLite-only periodic backups become a no-op.

nodes.label: Boot-Budget Gate for Rotation Tranches
nodes.rationale: A rotation is a forced restart, and a restart is where latent startup fragility surfaces — added after tandoor crash-looped six times on a 2m40s collectstatic against a 40s liveness budget with no startup probe. Having no startup probe mattered far less than the ratio of boot to budget; the apps that broke had NEGATIVE margin. Measured spread is real: pinepods came back at 156s against a measured 144s.

nodes.label: Rotation Cutover Burst Tracks Connection Churn, Not Pool Size
nodes.norm_label: rotation cutover burst tracks connection churn, not pool size
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL does not terminate existing sessions when a role's password changes, so windmill's 49 live pooled connections kept working and it logged only 4 failures despite the prediction of the loudest cutover. Only NEW connection attempts in the rotate-then-propagate gap fail. Reconnect rate is the right thing to look at, not pool size. Propagation lag is ~3 minutes (ESO refreshInterval) and looks like failure while you wait.
nodes.source_location: What the cutover burst actually tracks (corrected)

nodes.label: Three Mechanisms That Make a Rotated Password Take Effect
nodes.norm_label: three mechanisms that make a rotated password take effect
nodes.rationale: Stakater Reloader (annotation on the WORKLOAD, not the pod template — windmill's chart puts it on the pod template, which is why the estate looked covered and was not), Helm valuesFrom re-render, and the ESO reloader Config CR. Windmill's password ends up as a plaintext literal in the Deployment pod spec because valuesFrom/targetPath injects it at render time.
nodes.source_location: Prerequisite: every consuming workload must see a rotated password

nodes.label: Rotation Cannot Be Switched Off
nodes.rationale: rotation_period is mandatory (min 5s), OpenBao has no skip_import_rotation, and creating a static role rotates the password immediately. openbao#284 is still open. Every app in a tranche becomes a rotating-credential app permanently, with reloader-driven restarts on the rotation cadence.

nodes.label: Derived bazarr --cast List
nodes.rationale: The wiki gives four --cast flags; at 1.6.0 the schema has eleven DateTime columns because the page predates the release that moved subtitles into new tables. Generate from the schema bazarr just built. The pg_depend exclusion and relkind='r' are both load-bearing — the obvious information_schema version also returns pg_stat_statements extension VIEWS living in public, and casting those breaks the run. Also: POSTGRES_ENABLED must be the literal string 'true', POSTGRES_URL does not work alone, and bazarr's own backup task branches on the config.yaml key not the env var.

nodes.label: Blanket TRUNCATE of the Seeded Schema
nodes.norm_label: blanket truncate of the seeded schema
nodes.rationale: Prowlarr's wiki page has no DELETE step at all, which reads as an omission rather than a claim it seeds nothing. Truncating every table in public is a strict superset, identical in effect since pgloader reloads immediately, and cannot drift as the schema changes. RESTART IDENTITY resets the sequences the seed rows consumed and CASCADE means tables need not be named in foreign-key order. TRUNCATE is not DROP.

nodes.label: flux resume Does Not Restore the Replica Count
nodes.norm_label: flux resume does not restore the replica count
nodes.rationale: The app-template chart only renders replicas when it is configured, and none of these apps configure it, so Helm does not own that field and the scale-to-zero survives the resume untouched. `rollout status` then reports 'successfully rolled out' against zero replicas and you will believe the app is up. Verified on prowlarr, where exactly that happened.

nodes.label: Generic pg_get_serial_sequence Fix
nodes.rationale: The wiki's per-app setval lists pass NULL on an empty table, skip a value on every table (is_called defaults true), and drift — Sonarr's still reads Blacklist_Id_seq from Blocklist. Deriving every sequence from pg_get_serial_sequence cannot go stale. pgloader does reset sequences on its own, so this is belt-and-braces, but the failure it prevents is silent until the first insert.

nodes.label: Single-Schema (public) Drift Check
nodes.rationale: All eight apps emit unqualified DDL, so tables go wherever search_path resolves first. components/postgres declares only public and no role-named schema, so "$user" has nothing to resolve to. Not boilerplate for three of them: bazarr's 0124f9e278fb_ migration probes table_schema = 'public' and seerr's FixBlocklistIdDefault hard-codes public."blocklist_id_seq". A second row named after the app means the $user element has armed.

nodes.label: Suspending the HelmRelease Does Not Stop Reloader
nodes.norm_label: suspending the helmrelease does not stop reloader
nodes.rationale: Suspension stops Flux, not reloader, which patches the pod template the moment ${APP}-env first syncs — rolling the Deployment onto an EMPTY Postgres database past a suspended HelmRelease. Not hypothetical: on 2026-08-27 autobrr was the one app left running because it reuses its existing autobrr-oidc Secret, and it came up on an empty database and applied its own base schema. Scale-to-zero in the same breath is the only thing that closes it.
nodes.source_location: 4. Phase 1 — merge, and let the database and role land

nodes.label: Throwaway Schema-Init Pod with Different Labels
nodes.norm_label: throwaway schema-init pod with different labels
nodes.rationale: The wiki says run the app once against the empty databases; doing that with the real Deployment serves an empty library to Prowlarr's app sync, Pulsarr, Overseerr and anything else holding the API key. A bare Pod with deliberately DIFFERENT labels does not match the Service selector, and emptyDir for /config means it cannot find a SQLite file and has no choice but to build its schema in Postgres.
nodes.source_location: 5.2 Create the schema — in a throwaway pod, not the app

nodes.label: ralgar pgloader Build for the Overseerr Family
nodes.norm_label: ralgar pgloader build for the overseerr family
nodes.rationale: Both projects tell you to use ghcr.io/ralgar/pgloader:pr-1531 because stock releases mis-quote column identifiers on this schema — a community artifact from a patch that was never merged, so it is pinned to the OCI INDEX digest (which keeps kubectl doing platform selection) rather than the floating tag. DB_TYPE must be exactly 'postgres' (strict case-sensitive, no warning), and overriding the container command drops NODE_ENV=production so migrations silently never run. Keep the `migrations` table when truncating and expect pgloader to error on exactly that one table.

nodes.label: Startup Probe for Migration and Rotation Cold Boots
nodes.norm_label: startup probe for migration and rotation cold boots
nodes.rationale: All eight had ~110s of liveness budget and no startup probe. First boot against an empty Postgres database replays the entire migration chain, and every rotation forces a cold start — a kubelet kill mid-migration restarts the pod, which replays from the top, which gets killed again. A startup probe suspends liveness AND readiness until it passes; 60 x 10s buys ten minutes and costs nothing on a normal boot.
nodes.source_location: 2. What lands in git — The startup probe

nodes.label: Forward-Migrating a Stale SQLite Copy Before Loading
nodes.norm_label: forward-migrating a stale sqlite copy before loading
nodes.rationale: When the app was upgraded before the data was loaded, a data-only load does not just lose rows — it fails on renamed tables (jellyseerr blacklist -> blocklist). The fix is to migrate the SQLite COPY forward using the new image in SQLite mode. Four traps: the migrations land in the WAL so copy all three files; the image ignores SIGTERM and SIGKILL from kubectl exec; pkill -f matches its own shell; and opening the copy locally with sqlite3 checkpoints the WAL, which doubles as preparation.

nodes.label: OpenBao MCP Two-Hop Token Minting Design
nodes.norm_label: openbao mcp two-hop token minting design

nodes.label: externalDatabase wiring to the shared CNPG cluster
nodes.norm_label: externaldatabase wiring to the shared cnpg cluster

nodes.label: DEGOOG_DATA_DIR
nodes.rationale: Set explicitly rather than inherited from the working directory: plugins, engines, themes, server-settings.json and the indexer directory all derive from this one path (see paths.ts), so it is the single value that must agree with the volsync PVC mount point in helmrelease.yaml.

nodes.label: DEGOOG_VALKEY_URL (shared valkey db 9)
nodes.rationale: Points at the shared, password-less valkey in `database`. Database index 9 (8 is searxng, 6 is dispatcharr); degoog already namespaces keys by instance identifier, so the distinct index is tidiness that keeps a stray FLUSHDB from taking two apps down.

nodes.label: FlareSolverr Sidecar
nodes.rationale: A degoog transport backend running real Chrome to solve Cloudflare interstitials. Kept as a sidecar rather than its own app: degoog is the only consumer, and same-pod means the transport URL is http://127.0.0.1:8191/v1 with no Service, no route and no ingress. It gets plain env rather than envFrom degoog-env so a browser sandbox never holds the database password. The Store extension itself is NOT deployed by this file — installing it is a settings-page step.

nodes.label: Degoog search.* HTTPRoute (local-user)
nodes.rationale: Hostname is `search`, not `degoog`; TAILSCALE_HOST in ks.yaml carries the same name onto the tailnet. The route filters through the `local-user` Traefik middleware — a network gate with no authentik outpost.

nodes.label: Retrom Dropped Postgres Component
nodes.rationale: The components/postgres line is commented out rather than deleted because the whole ks.yaml is parked (group E drop, 2026-08-25). The Database CR, the database and the login role were all removed, so re-enabling the line does not restore the old state: the Pulumi `system` stack discovers the component and creates database/static-roles/${APP}, which fails outright until CNPG has recreated the login role.

nodes.label: Romm Gatus Low-Power Maintenance Window
nodes.rationale: Romm is scaled to 0 between 02:00 and 09:00 by the nightly Low Power shed (docs/cluster-consolidation/24-power-states.md), so a failed Gatus check inside that window is expected rather than an incident. Gatus keeps checking and keeps the history; it just does not alert.

nodes.label: Romm Startup Probe Widening
nodes.rationale: The startup probe was widened from failureThreshold 3 (a 30s budget) to 300s ahead of putting romm's password on OpenBao rotation: a rotation is a forced restart and the pod's own conditions show Initialized->Ready taking 49s. tandoor (#1142) crash-looped six times on exactly this shape. Startup probes suppress liveness and readiness while pending, so this only widens the boot window; steady state is unchanged. Do not narrow it back.

nodes.label: Degoog Authentik Forward Proxy
nodes.rationale: Forward proxy rather than oauth2 because degoog has no OIDC support at all; its only authentication is DEGOOG_SETTINGS_PASSWORDS, which gates the settings/extension panel and nothing else. The HTTPRoute still filters through `local-user`, a network gate WITHOUT the authentik outpost hop, because a search engine must answer OpenSearch and ?q= requests straight from the browser address bar and an outpost redirect breaks both. Same shape as searxng.

nodes.label: Degoog Gatus Low-Power Maintenance Window
nodes.rationale: Degoog is scaled to 0 between 02:00 and 09:00 by the nightly Low Power shed, so failed checks in that window are expected and suppressed from alerting. The check targets /healthz rather than / so it does not run an actual search, and the route's own rate limiter applies to it.

nodes.label: DEGOOG_DISTRUST_PROXY Setting
nodes.rationale: Set to 0 (trust the proxy) — the variable is named for the negative, so the default of 1 makes degoog ignore X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP and every client looks like the Traefik pod, collapsing degoog's rate limiting and IP blocklist onto one source address. Safe only because the HTTPRoute through the internal gateway is the sole ingress path.

nodes.label: DEGOOG_POSTGRES Connection String
nodes.rationale: Built by hand instead of using the postgres_uri key, because that key carries ?sslmode=disable and degoog's driver (postgres.js 3.4.9) does `query.sslmode && (query.ssl = query.sslmode)` — the string "disable" is truthy, so the client opens TLS with rejectUnauthorized at its default, which fails against CNPG's self-signed CA and leaves the indexer silently at `adapter boot failed`. Omitting the query string keeps postgres.js at ssl: false, the plaintext connection every other app in the namespace makes to postgres-rw.

nodes.label: DEGOOG_SETTINGS_PASSWORDS
nodes.rationale: Read only from the environment — there is no settings UI or on-disk file for it. Left unset, degoog mints a throwaway password per process and prints it to the log, so on a restarting pod the admin panel password changes without warning; that panel installs extensions, and extensions run code on the server.

nodes.label: FlareSolverr /dev/shm tmpfs
nodes.rationale: Kubernetes gives 64Mi of /dev/shm and Chrome uses shared memory for renderer surfaces; past that it crashes mid-challenge and reads as a FlareSolverr timeout. Sized 512Mi rather than the usual 2Gi because `medium: Memory` counts against the container's own memory limit and a larger tmpfs could be filled to OOM the 1536Mi container. Mounted with advancedMounts so it applies only to flaresolverr.

nodes.label: Degoog Entrypoint Bypass (bun run)
nodes.rationale: The image ENTRYPOINT is bypassed with an explicit `bun run src/server/index.ts` command: entrypoint.sh does mkdir/chown on /app/data then su-exec, all of which need to start as uid 0 since the image sets no USER. fsGroup already makes the PVC group-writable by 1000, so the chown is redundant. Safe without a writable HOME because the image sets BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0.

nodes.label: Degoog /readyz Readiness Probe
nodes.rationale: Readiness targets /readyz rather than /healthz: degoog answers /healthz as soon as the HTTP server binds and only flips /readyz once markReady() runs at the end of boot, which is after the Postgres indexer adapter has connected.

nodes.label: Shared uid 1000 Pod SecurityContext
nodes.rationale: uid 1000 suits both containers by coincidence: degoog's base is oven/bun (user `bun`, uid 1000) and FlareSolverr's Dockerfile runs a bare useradd on python:3.11-slim, taking the first free id, also 1000. The numeric value is load-bearing because FlareSolverr's image declares USER by name, and with runAsNonRoot: true and no numeric override the kubelet refuses to start it.

nodes.label: New-App Postgres Ordering Trap (#1180)
nodes.rationale: Degoog is the app that found the new-app ordering trap: stacks/system raced Flux to the merge commit and died on `role "degoog" does not exist`. Read the ORDER OF OPERATIONS block in components/postgres/ks.yaml before adding components/postgres to a NEW app. The rotating credential is preflighted the way freshrss was — reloader.stakater.com/auto on the controller plus the credential arriving via the degoog-env Secret.

nodes.label: discoverPostgresApps() Repository Discovery
nodes.rationale: Globs kubernetes/apps/**/ks.yaml and PARSES YAML spec.components, matching the path exactly so sibling components are not double-counted — which is why it correctly excludes autobrr's commented-out line where a shell grep counts it. But it never checks whether a parent kustomization actually includes that ks.yaml, so commented-out apps still count. Take the app list from this function, never from grep.
nodes.source_location: The app list is discovered, not typed

nodes.label: Client Certificate CN Comes from DatabaseRole spec.name
nodes.norm_label: client certificate cn comes from databaserole spec.name
nodes.rationale: The Secret is named <metadata.name>-client-cert, but issueClientCertificate calls generateCertificateFromCA with role.Spec.Name. PostgreSQL cert auth maps CN onto the role name, so spec.name is the field that has to be right.

nodes.label: 2.4b — Remove the Password Rollback
nodes.rationale: disablePassword: true, delete the sops document, delete openbao-credentials.yaml, and hostnossl openbao openbao all reject — done as ONE change after a soak, because any one of them removes the ability to fall back. The soak gate was met in the sense the plan intended: the replicas cold-started on cert auth 90 minutes after the certificate was issued.

nodes.label: openbao-replica-dump Nightly pg_dump CronJob
nodes.rationale: Had to be moved onto the client certificate BEFORE disablePassword, or the failure would surface at 03:00 rather than at merge. It was authenticating with the password AND sslmode=disable, so both halves of 2.4b would have rejected it independently. pg_dump is libpq, which DOES enforce key permissions, unlike pgx.

nodes.label: baoadmin — Certificate-Only Superuser Rotation Identity
nodes.rationale: No passwordSecret, no disablePassword — the certificate is the only way in from the moment the role exists, so there is no bootstrap password and no rotate-root ceremony. Superuser is not a choice: PG16+ restricts CREATEROLE password changes to ADMIN OPTION holders and CNPG's inRoles issues a plain GRANT, so a least-privilege rotator is unreachable declaratively. Mitigated by keeping `postgres` sops-backed and outside OpenBao's reach as break-glass. Separate Secret and separate mount (/etc/pg-admin-certs) from the storage cert so a superuser key is never one sslcert= typo away.

nodes.label: OpenBao database Secrets Engine (stacks/system)
nodes.rationale: Two switches meaning different things: ENGINE_ENABLED decides whether the mount exists (off until the pulumi policy is widened, because stacks/system publishes clusters/<key>/details that every other stack reads); ROTATION_TRANCHE decides which apps get a static role, and creating one rotates immediately with no opt-out. Certificate PATHS not inline PEM, so the baoadmin private key never enters Pulumi state or the Minio backend. database/creds/* is deliberately withheld so dynamic roles are a 403 rather than silent design drift.

nodes.label: passwords.sops.yaml Retirement
nodes.rationale: Phase 4's line 'delete passwords.sops.yaml' was wrong as written: each <app>-postgres-password Secret carries database/hostname/password/port/username and the OpenBao generator returns only username and password. Retiring the file needed the connection metadata REHOMED first (to <app>-postgres-conn, #1176), then the documents could go. 19 documents down to 2; every surviving document was fingerprinted before and compared after.
nodes.source_location: passwords.sops.yaml is down to two documents

nodes.label: components/postgres/rotate Folded into the Base Component
nodes.norm_label: components/postgres/rotate folded into the base component
nodes.rationale: The staging the sibling provided had done its job across nine tranches, and by then components/postgres ALONE was a broken configuration: no <app>-postgres-password document existed any more, so the base component's passwordSecret pointed at a Secret that could not exist. A new app that forgot the rotate line would silently never get a role.

nodes.label: Talos API CA Rotation
nodes.rationale: Talos has no CRL, so rotating the CA is the ONLY way to revoke a client certificate — issuing a replacement admin cert does not invalidate the old one. Written after a talosconfig carrying an os:admin cert and its unencrypted ED25519 key was committed to a public repo. --kubernetes=false is deliberate: a leaked talosconfig is a Talos-API credential with its own blast radius.

nodes.label: OpenBao Postgres Client-Certificate Credential
nodes.rationale: OpenBao stores its own state in the shared CNPG cluster, so its database credential is the one credential in the estate that cannot come from OpenBao. A CNPG-issued client certificate beats generating a password and pushing it into KV: nothing to store, it DELETES objects (openbao-postgres ExternalSecret, openbao-storage ExternalSecret, the sops password document) rather than adding them, and CNPG already authenticates streaming_replica this way.

nodes.label: defaultMode 0400 Lands as 0440 via fsGroup
nodes.rationale: kubelet ORs the pod's fsGroup group-read bit into the volume mode, so 0400 becomes r--r----- owned by group 1000. It does not matter for pgx, which does os.ReadFile with no permission check — but it does matter for libpq (pg_dump), and without an fsGroup the files are root-owned and unreadable by the app uid.

nodes.label: ESO ClusterSecretStore Instead of Reflector for Cross-Namespace Certs
nodes.norm_label: eso clustersecretstore instead of reflector for cross-namespace certs
nodes.rationale: Reflector requires reflection-allowed annotation ON THE SOURCE, even in explicit reflects: mode. Both source Secrets (openbao-client-cert, postgres-ca) are created by the CNPG operator, not Flux, so nothing in git can annotate them. ClusterSecretStore/database reads the namespace directly and is already the path openbao-storage used.

nodes.label: hostssl Rule Inertness Property
nodes.rationale: pg_hba matches on connection type, so a hostssl rule cannot match a non-SSL connection. Adding `hostssl openbao openbao all cert` while the connection URL still says sslmode=disable changes nothing about the running system, which makes the cutover a one-line change with a database-free rollback. Proven live via pg_stat_ssl joined to pg_stat_activity: six openbao connections, ssl=f, no client DN.
nodes.source_location: The property that makes this safe

nodes.label: Orphaned openbao-postgres ExternalSecret Feeds the Nightly Dump
nodes.norm_label: orphaned openbao-postgres externalsecret feeds the nightly dump
nodes.rationale: The prune guard and deletionPolicy: Orphan kept the object alive but nothing in git declared it, so the next person tidying orphans would have taken the nightly openbao-replica-dump with them. The fix was to RE-DECLARE it in openbao-credentials.yaml, not to delete it.

nodes.label: pgx Caches the Client Certificate at Process Start
nodes.norm_label: pgx caches the client certificate at process start
nodes.rationale: pgx builds the client certificate into tlsConfig.Certificates inside configTLS, which runs once during ParseConfig at sql.Open. A renewed certificate on disk is invisible to a running OpenBao process, so renewal must ride on a restart. This is the finding that forces a volume mount rather than any other delivery mechanism.

nodes.label: Reloader-Driven Certificate Renewal Path
nodes.rationale: Three hops: CNPG patches openbao-client-cert in `database`, ESO re-syncs it into kube-system on an hourly refresh, and only then does reloader see the change and roll the StatefulSet. reloader.stakater.com/auto belongs on the WORKLOAD only; it is meaningless on a Secret or ConfigMap.

nodes.label: Group E — Disabled Apps Leave Their Databases Behind
nodes.norm_label: group e — disabled apps leave their databases behind
nodes.rationale: outline, retrom and strmgen were commented out of their parent kustomization so no Flux Kustomization managed them, yet their CNPG Database CRs survived because components/postgres sets deletionPolicy: Orphan on its nested Kustomization. Disabling an app in the repo therefore leaves its database behind, silently. Order matters when dropping: CRs first (databaseReclaimPolicy: retain), then DROP DATABASE, then DROP ROLE — reversed, the controller recreates the database underneath you.

nodes.label: Pulumi SecretsMount URN Re-Parenting Incident
nodes.rationale: Re-parenting the SecretsMount into a PostgresRotationComponent changed its URN, which Pulumi reads as a different resource: create new, delete old. The create failed on 'path is already in use', which was the lucky outcome — a success would have unmounted database/ and taken every static role with it. Never resolve this by unmounting to 'clear' the path. aliases: [{noParent: true}] did NOT work; only the full old URN string did.

nodes.label: Brand-New App Ordering Trap (SQLSTATE 42704)
nodes.rationale: Two constraints point opposite ways: a MIGRATED app needs the Kubernetes half before the Pulumi run (the reverse rotates a password the app cannot read); a BRAND-NEW app needs the PostgreSQL login role before the Pulumi run or stacks/system fails outright on `role "x" does not exist`. Pulumi reliably wins the race against Flux's cluster-apps interval. Not made self-healing deliberately: the check would need cluster state, and an app omitted from the tranche is DELETED not skipped, so a transient read failure would destroy a live app's static role. Loud-and-stuck is the better failure.

nodes.label: Split-Brain on Postgres Restore
nodes.rationale: Restoring Postgres from Barman brings roles back with backup-time passwords while OpenBao holds snapshot-time ones, locking every app out. Recovery is a loop of `bao write -f database/rotate-role/<name>`. This is also why the postgres superuser stays in sops and outside OpenBao's reach.

nodes.label: Proving the Old Certificate Is Dead Is the Gate
nodes.norm_label: proving the old certificate is dead is the gate
nodes.rationale: A rotation you have not proven rejects the old certificate has not remediated anything — the gate is the old talosconfig failing, not step 2 completing. The leaked blob stays retrievable from public git history by SHA, which is harmless once the cert no longer authenticates; do not treat history rewriting as the fix and skip rotation.
nodes.source_location: 6. Confirm the leaked credential is dead

nodes.label: rotate-ca Does Not Update talsecret.sops.yaml
nodes.rationale: talosctl rotate-ca generates a fresh secrets bundle internally and cannot accept an existing one (siderolabs/talos#12816, --with-secrets not implemented). This cluster is talhelper-managed, so after a rotation talsecret.sops.yaml still holds the OLD CA and the next genconfig + apply-config pushes it back, undoing the rotation or leaving nodes split-trust. Updating the file is a required step, not cleanup.

nodes.label: authenticated-user Middleware chain
nodes.rationale: Standard gated chain: error-pages -> outpost -> internal-network. Ordering matters -- error-pages wraps first so an outpost or IP rejection renders a themed page rather than a bare 401/403.

nodes.label: local-user Middleware chain
nodes.rationale: The authenticated-user chain minus the outpost hop: error-pages -> internal-network. Exists so break-glass surfaces (notably the Traefik dashboard) can be network-gated without a dependency on authentik being up.

nodes.label: cloudflare-ips ipAllowList Middleware
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare's published v4/v6 ranges, plus the RFC1918 and tailnet ranges inlined because Traefik chains do not support OR operations (traefik/traefik#6007) -- the union has to live inside a single ipAllowList rather than being composed from two.

nodes.label: crowdsec-bouncer-plugin Middleware
nodes.rationale: Named crowdsec-bouncer-plugin, NOT crowdsec-bouncer: components/common/middleware.yaml defines a per-namespace alias of that name and `network` includes components/common like every other namespace, so both manifests targeted network/crowdsec-bouncer, the alias won, and the plugin config was overwritten by a chain pointing at itself ('recursion detected in middleware'), after which Traefik dropped every router carrying the filter. The plugin key must also match experimental.plugins in values.yaml (crowdsec-bouncer-traefik-plugin) -- it previously read crowdsec-bouncer and could never resolve to a loaded plugin.

nodes.label: error-pages Middleware
nodes.rationale: Catches 401-599 and rewrites to /{status}.html against the error-pages Service in the network namespace on port 8080 -- the Traefik-side half of the error-pages HelmRelease deployment.

nodes.label: fail2ban plugin Middleware
nodes.rationale: Bans on 4 failures in 10m for 12h against status codes 400,401,403-499, with the same five internal ranges allowlisted -- but as a comma-separated scalar rather than a list. Commented out of middleware/kustomization.yaml, so it is not applied; it is the older in-Traefik answer to the same abuse-blocking problem the CrowdSec bouncer now owns.

nodes.label: github-hook-ips ipAllowList Middleware
nodes.rationale: GitHub's webhook source ranges from https://api.github.com/meta, maintained by hand -- narrows webhook receivers to GitHub only, with no internal ranges added (unlike cloudflare-ips).

nodes.label: internal-network ipAllowList Middleware
nodes.rationale: Allows CLUSTER_NETWORK, SERVICE_NETWORK, RFC1918 10/8 and 192.168/16, and the tailnet CGNAT range 100.64/10 -- the same five-range set repeated in cloudflare-ips, fail2ban's allowlist, the crowdsec trusted-IP lists, and the values.yaml forwardedHeaders trustedIPs.

nodes.label: outpost forwardAuth Middleware
nodes.rationale: forwardAuth to authentik-outpost.${CLUSTER_CNAME}:9000 with trustForwardHeader, propagating the full X-authentik-* header set (including the JWT and JWKS metadata) plus Remote-User so downstream apps can do header-based SSO.

nodes.label: traefik-tls-settings ConfigMap
nodes.rationale: Delivers store.yaml to Traefik's file provider (--providers.file.filename=/config/store.yaml) declaring both /certs (le-production-tls) and /cluster-certs (cluster-tls) certificates, with the Let's Encrypt pair as the default store certificate.

nodes.label: CrowdSec bouncer kill switch and fail-open posture
nodes.norm_label: crowdsec bouncer kill switch and fail-open posture
nodes.rationale: `enabled: false` is the standing rollback for every enforcement stage, because middlewares attach per-route via ExtensionRef across 74 HTTPRoutes in 69 files -- detaching at that scale is not a rollback. It does NOT skip validation: the plugin runs ValidateParams unconditionally in New(), so an empty crowdsecLapiKeyFile breaks every referencing route regardless. Deliberately fail-open: crowdsecMode stream (a LAPI outage degrades to a stale list instead of sitting in the request path), streamStartupBlock false (default true would block traffic during init until first sync), updateMaxFailure -1 (default 0 turns a LAPI restart into a 403 storm), httpTimeoutSeconds 3, remediationStatusCode 403 so a false-positive ban is distinguishable from a 5xx. Stated trade-off: fail-open makes a wrong bouncer key indistinguishable from 'no decisions' -- `cscli bouncers list` showing a recent Last API pull is the only positive proof. forwardedHeadersTrustedIPs (which proxies to trust for XFF) and clientTrustedIPs (which resolved clients to never evaluate) do different jobs; the latter is the break-glass escape hatch that survives a sick LAPI. defaultDecisionSeconds is deliberately unset -- live-mode only.

nodes.label: crowdsecLapiKeyFile / 1Password field-name coupling
nodes.rationale: The 1Password field `apikey_bouncer` on item 'Crowdsec ApiKey' is synced into the crowdsec-secret Secret by traefik/crowdsec-secret.yaml and mounted at /etc/secrets/crowdsec by values.yaml. The 1Password operator syncs field names verbatim with no rename facility, so the file name IS the field name. This previously pointed at /etc/secrets/crowdsec/lapi, a name that exists nowhere; it was repointed rather than introducing an ExternalSecret whose only job would be renaming, which would be a second mapping to keep in sync -- how it broke in the first place. The LAPI reads the same field as BOUNCER_KEY_traefik, so both ends are the same field by construction.

nodes.rationale: multus is a CNI DaemonSet: a node without it cannot attach secondary interfaces, so it must tolerate the control-plane taint that arrives with allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes: false. The patch REPLACES the whole tolerations list, so CriticalAddonsOnly is repeated to preserve it; re-diff against the chart's hardcodedValues when bumping the pinned digest.

Both controllers.multus.pod.tolerations and defaultPodOptions.tolerations were rendered locally with helm template and silently ignored, so the rendered manifest (postRenderer) is the only lever.

nodes.label: ESO over reflector for CNPG-created Secrets
nodes.norm_label: eso over reflector for cnpg-created secrets
nodes.rationale: Both source Secrets are created by the CNPG operator, not Flux, so nothing in git can put reflector's reflection-allowed annotation on them — and reflector's explicit reflects: mode still requires it on the source. ClusterSecretStore/database is a kubernetes provider reading the database namespace directly. Everything lands in ONE Secret so there is one volume to mount and one object for reloader to watch, which matters because pgx reads the cert into tls.Config once at ParseConfig.

nodes.label: Superuser certificate kept in a separate Secret and mount
nodes.norm_label: superuser certificate kept in a separate secret and mount
nodes.rationale: openbao-pg-client-cert is the unprivileged storage identity; openbao-pg-admin-cert is a PostgreSQL superuser. Sharing a directory would put a superuser key one sslcert= typo away from the storage connection, and would make 'which cert does this path hold' a question rather than a fact.

nodes.label: Prohibition on disable_unauthed_generate_root_endpoints
nodes.rationale: Opened twice (#3067, #3078) because minting a root token from recovery shares had no other route; each time it meant two pod rolls and a public root-generation endpoint in between. Fixed by a break-glass AppRole whose only capability is opening an attempt on the authenticated endpoint (deny on secret reads and policy writes), with completion still requiring 3 of 5 recovery shares.

nodes.label: Certificate mounted as a volume so renewal rolls the pod
nodes.norm_label: certificate mounted as a volume so renewal rolls the pod
nodes.rationale: pgx reads the cert into its tls.Config once during ParseConfig at sql.Open, so a renewed certificate on disk is invisible to a running process. reloader.stakater.com/auto + RollingUpdate turns a renewal into a restart, and reloader only sees Secrets the pod actually mounts. defaultMode 0400 is hardening, not a requirement: pgx does os.ReadFile straight into tls.X509KeyPair with no permission check, unlike libpq.

nodes.label: RollingUpdate + reloader on the StatefulSet
nodes.rationale: Config is a ConfigMap read once at process start, so a config-only change leaves the pod template untouched and servers keep serving the OLD config while Flux reports success — that bit the OIDC bootstrap for 15h. Reloader rolls the StatefulSet on ConfigMap change, but is inert under the chart's default OnDelete strategy (the controller never replaces pods, and kubectl rollout restart refuses outright). OnDelete is right for Shamir-sealed upstream Vault; here transit auto-unseal makes rolling safe.

nodes.label: OpenBao is never a link in the chain that starts OpenBao
nodes.norm_label: openbao is never a link in the chain that starts openbao
nodes.rationale: external-secrets is a dependency only for ClusterSecretStore/database, a kubernetes provider reading the database namespace — not backed by 1Password today nor by OpenBao later. The seal token, which has no in-cluster source, comes from secret.sops.yaml. tailscale-services is a dependency because the unseal path runs through the dockge-as egress Service, without which pods crash-loop on a seal they cannot reach. Flipping suspend to false is a one-way go-live decision: the database will have been written to.

nodes.label: Two secret-bearing values, two deliberate sources
nodes.norm_label: two secret-bearing values, two deliberate sources
nodes.rationale: The Postgres connection URL comes from ExternalSecret via ClusterSecretStore/database so it rotates with the role without a second edit; the transit token comes from secret.sops.yaml because nothing in the cluster can regenerate it — it is minted against bao-transit and mirrored at bootstrap/openbao/transit-token.sops.yaml per bootstrap/INVENTORY.md. Everything else about the server config is plaintext in helmrelease.yaml.

nodes.label: Estate-wide shared rclone SFTP keypair
nodes.rationale: The same keypair DockgeLxc seeds onto every dockge host; its public half is already in authorized_keys on dockge-as, so shipping dumps needs no new key material anywhere. OpenSSH refuses a key file without a trailing newline, so the template appends one (DockgeLxc.ts:247 does the same).

nodes.label: Dump/restore trust boundary (no age identity on alpha-site)
nodes.norm_label: dump/restore trust boundary (no age identity on alpha-site)
nodes.rationale: Both cronjobs run in-cluster rather than on alpha-site so the dump can never be decryptable on alpha-site alone — that host also holds the transit key. The cluster already holds an age identity (Flux sops-age), so decrypting here adds no new exposure, and the restore test doubles as proof the dump left the building and can be fetched back. An unverified backup is not a backup (RUNBOOK Scenario D).

nodes.label: Gatus heartbeat via dockge-as egress with --connect-to
nodes.norm_label: gatus heartbeat via dockge-as egress with --connect-to
nodes.rationale: Pods have no route to the tailnet and no reachable DNS answer for uptime.${ROOT_DOMAIN}; Gatus is reported to through the dockge-as egress on 443, with --connect-to keeping Host/SNI intact so Traefik routes and the LE cert validates.

nodes.label: Literal PG_URI with client-certificate authentication
nodes.rationale: The dump used to authenticate with the openbao role's password over sslmode=disable; Phase 2.4b nulls that password and adds 'hostnossl openbao openbao all reject', either of which would break the job silently at 03:00. A certificate URI carries no secret so it needs no ExternalSecret — the credential is the mounted key. libpq enforces private-key permissions where pgx does not, so this was verified live (ssl=true, TLSv1.3, pg_dump exit=0) rather than assumed.

nodes.label: PGDATA subdirectory fix for Postgres 18 images
nodes.norm_label: pgdata subdirectory fix for postgres 18 images
nodes.rationale: Postgres 18 images refuse to start when the mount IS the data directory ('unused mount/volume'), and the pgdata emptyDir mounts exactly there. Pointing PGDATA at a subdirectory of the mount is the fix, matching docker/_common/postgres. Renovate crossed this major on its own once and broke the job silently for weeks (#835), which is why a renovate guard blocks majors for this image. Plain-SQL dumps restore into any equal-or-newer major, so the scratch engine only has to be >= the dump's origin major.

nodes.label: Deliberate omission of the postgres component
nodes.norm_label: deliberate omission of the postgres component
nodes.rationale: This app reads the existing openbao database with the credential provisioned for the openbao app; adding components/postgres would declare a SECOND database, role and credential named after this app. It dependsOn the openbao ks (not just postgres) so a half-initialised database is never dumped during bootstrap, and on tailscale-services because ports 2023/8200/443 to alpha-site exist only through the dockge-as egress Service.

nodes.label: Three-trust-root credential routing
nodes.rationale: ExternalSecret supplies the Postgres credential and the SFTP key (referenced, never copied); SOPS supplies the restore-test AppRole because it has no other in-cluster source; the transit seal token and the age identity are referenced from Secrets owned elsewhere (openbao-seal, sops-age) so a re-minted token never needs a second edit here.

nodes.label: Three estate age recipients
nodes.rationale: Must stay identical to .sops.yaml in this repo, vault, and stargate-command-cluster — a divergent set is how a dump becomes undecryptable by the one key that survives. No alpha-site-resident key is ever added: the host holding the ciphertext (and the transit key) must not be able to decrypt it alone.

nodes.label: Deliberate priority-value ordering for the low-power tier
nodes.norm_label: deliberate priority-value ordering for the low-power tier
nodes.rationale: Below system-cluster-critical (2000000000) and longhorn-critical (1000000000), above observability-critical (1000) and every unset pod. Priority governs preemption under contention, not placement: with workers powered off Tier-2 pods simply go Pending. The value of the class is the case where a control plane is LOST mid-window and the two survivors must evict the right things. Three same-named-looking objects, three kinds: this PriorityClass critical-tier, Longhorn's PriorityClass longhorn-critical, and piece 12's StorageClass longhorn-critical.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization ${APP}-postgres-databases
nodes.rationale: A separate Flux Kustomization exists because a Flux Kustomization has exactly one spec.path, and a CNPG Database is namespace-scoped with spec.cluster.name as a local reference, so the object must land in the `database` namespace next to the Cluster. The app's own Kustomization cannot do it because targetNamespace is Kustomize's namespace transformer and overrides an explicitly-set metadata.namespace. Keeping it separate also means a broken extra-database manifest still leaves the app its own database, login role and credential. Depends on postgres-operator rather than the postgres cluster Kustomization to avoid the openbao/postgres cold-boot readiness cycle; wait:false for the same reason; deletionPolicy Orphan so an ownership change never cascade-deletes a database.

nodes.label: postgres/databases Component
nodes.rationale: components/postgres renders exactly ONE Database named after the app; some applications need a second (a log or cache database with a different retention/vacuum profile, or a vendor hard-coding two connection strings). Consumers are sonarr, radarr, lidarr, prowlarr (<app>-log). Before this component the options were all bad: grant the app superuser so it can CREATE DATABASE, create it by hand and leave it undeclared, or fold a second Database into ../database where every app would get one. Deliberately invisible to Pulumi rotation discovery (stacks/system/postgres-rotation.ts matches components/postgres by exact path suffix) because an extra database reuses the app's existing role and needs no static role.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization ${APP}-postgres-roles
nodes.rationale: Renders <app-dir>/postgres-roles/ into the `database` namespace. A DatabaseRole is namespace-scoped with spec.cluster.name a local reference so it must land beside the Cluster, and the app's own Kustomization cannot put it there because targetNamespace overrides metadata.namespace. Separate from ${APP}-postgres because a Flux Kustomization has exactly one spec.path. The directory must NOT be listed in the app's own kustomization.yaml or the roles render a second time into the app's namespace.

nodes.label: postgres/roles Component
nodes.rationale: Some applications' migrations reference roles they do not create — grant targets, RLS principals, ownership handles — assuming the migration runs as something holding CREATEROLE, which app roles here deliberately are not (login:true and nothing else). Consumers: toolhive-registry (toolhive_registry_server) and windmill (windmill_user, windmill_admin). Before this component the options were: hand the app superuser for a single statement, grant CREATEROLE permanently, or create the roles by hand — which is what happened to windmill, and why its two roles existed in the cluster and in no manifest.

nodes.label: postgres/superuser Component
nodes.rationale: Opts an app's database role into PostgreSQL superuser. It is a component rather than a POSTGRES_SUPERUSER substitution because a boolean cannot travel through postBuild.substitute — that field is typed map[string]string, a bare false is rejected by the Kustomization CRD, and quoting it in source does not survive kustomize build. Works by patching the nested ${APP}-postgres Kustomization to carry its own spec.patches entry, which Flux then applies to the DatabaseRole: two levels of patch, one level of indirection each.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization cluster-apps
nodes.rationale: Owns the entire ./kubernetes/apps apply set and depends on cluster-meta. Its blanket patch adds SOPS decryption and postBuild.substituteFrom (cluster-secrets, cluster-versions, shared-secrets) to every child Kustomization, which is why per-app substituteFrom lists are always dead.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization cluster-meta
nodes.rationale: The Flux root's meta layer (./kubernetes/flux/meta), ported from equestria-cluster for piece 21 Phase B and made live at the Phase C root flip. prune was false across the flip so an incomplete tree would surface as drift rather than garbage collection; restored 2026-08-14 only after the flip settled, 16 -ref stubs were deleted by hand, cluster-apps re-owned all 155 children, and a dry run showed 401 rendered objects against 401 inventory entries with zero difference. targetNamespace is hardcoded flux-system because Renovate lookups require it.

nodes.label: driscoll.dev/backup-credentials annotation requirement
nodes.rationale: The postgres-backup CronJob enumerates Database resources in the `database` namespace and for each reads the credential Secret this annotation names, defaulting to `<database>-postgres` — which for an extra database does not exist. Without the annotation the nightly run fails on a Secret that was never going to be there, and one failed database exits the whole job non-zero, at 02:00. Replaces an older three-document pattern (Database + <db>-postgres-conn Secret + duplicate ExternalSecret) with one line where the database is declared.

nodes.label: Postgres component family never prunes
nodes.rationale: The nested ks is deletionPolicy: Orphan and each Database carries databaseReclaimPolicy: retain plus kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/prune: disabled, so removing a file leaves the live database alone. `ensure: absent` DROPS the database and everything in it and is not a synonym for deleting the manifest. CNPG also will not recreate a database that disappears underneath it — it gates on observedGeneration == generation and no-ops even with ensure: present; force a reconcile by toggling spec.allowConnections.

nodes.label: Extra databases use only the public schema
nodes.norm_label: extra databases use only the public schema
nodes.rationale: A schema named after the role arms the dormant `$user` element of the default search_path and shadows public, splitting the app's data across two schemas. Extra databases therefore declare only `public`, owned by the app's own login role.

nodes.label: DatabaseRole adopts and forces every attribute
nodes.norm_label: databaserole adopts and forces every attribute
nodes.rationale: A DatabaseRole adopts an existing role and forces EVERY attribute to match the manifest, including omitted ones. Because these roles are frequently created by hand before being declared, read the live role first (pg_roles and pg_auth_members) and match it exactly. windmill_admin carries BYPASSRLS and is a member of windmill_user; declaring it without either silently strips a privilege the application's row security depends on.

nodes.label: POSTGRES_APP_PATH anchor idiom
nodes.rationale: A Flux Kustomization's spec.path is repo-root-relative and a component rendered into an app's build has no idea where that build came from — kustomize does not expose it. ${APP} is not enough because an app's directory is not derivable from its name (windmill under equestria/home, toolhive-registry under agents). So the app hands its own path down via `path: &path ...` / `POSTGRES_APP_PATH: *path`, written once so a moved app cannot end up with a stale path. postBuild substitution is textual over the whole rendered output, so it reaches spec.path like any other field. Forgetting the variable renders a bare `/postgres-roles` and fails with path-not-found — deliberate, so opting in without wiring the path says so. The same variable is read by the databases sibling, so an app using both passes it once.

nodes.label: JSON6902 append instead of strategic merge on spec.patches
nodes.norm_label: json6902 append instead of strategic merge on spec.patches
nodes.rationale: A Flux Kustomization is a CRD with no Go schema, so kustomize applies a JSON merge patch where a list REPLACES rather than merges — two sibling components each setting spec.patches meant the second silently won. A JSON6902 `op: add` to `/spec/patches/-` appends and composes. The target is scoped by the name regex `.*-postgres$` so it cannot reach a Flux Kustomization emitted by another component of the same app.

nodes.label: cluster-versions three-site coupling
nodes.rationale: cluster-versions is generated by components/common's configMapGenerator from a repo-root versions.env. Three sites must change together: versions.env, the generator plus both substituteFrom lists in components/common, and the entry in this root patch. substituteFrom is not optional by default, so a reference without a generator fails EVERY child Kustomization with 'ConfigMap/cluster-versions not found', while a generator without references silently substitutes nothing. It could not simply be dropped because the versions feed tuppr's Talos and Kubernetes upgrades — those CRs currently hold literal versions with their own renovate annotations, so nothing would break immediately, but removing the mechanism would foreclose collapsing that duplication onto one source of truth.

nodes.label: Secret: technitium-pkcs12-password
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a plaintext literal ('technitium') rather than a real secret: it only protects the keystore file inside the cluster, and the same value must be typed into the Technitium API as the per-node certificate password after the node joins.

nodes.label: Certificate: technitium-tls
nodes.rationale: letsencrypt-production cert for ${CLUSTER_CNAME}.dns.${ROOT_DOMAIN} with a PKCS12 keystore, because Technitium's per-node cluster TLS wants a pkcs12 file rather than a PEM pair.

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: technitium-env
nodes.rationale: Pulls the admin password from the shared apps/technitium/admin path but the OIDC triple from the per-cluster clusters/equestria/apps/technitium/oidc path; deletionPolicy Retain keeps DNS alive if OpenBao is sealed.

nodes.label: tailscale sidecar (dns-${CLUSTER_CNAME})
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a sidecar rather than the Tailscale operator's L3 ingress: the operator could only ever serve INBOUND traffic, but Technitium's outbound cluster traffic (zone refresh, config sync, heartbeats) must source from the same registered tailnet IP. TS_KUBE_SECRET is blanked so state lives on the volsync PVC (subPath .tailscale-state) instead of a kube Secret, and TS_ACCEPT_DNS is false so the cluster resolver stays intact.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: technitium
nodes.rationale: Runs as root with NET_BIND_SERVICE so it can hold :53, attaches the technitium-dns-net ipvlan NAD for direct LAN DNS, and keeps its DNS_SERVER_* env in lockstep with docker/_common/technitium/.env — those vars are first-start-only once /etc/dns exists, after which cluster sync owns the settings.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: technitium
nodes.rationale: Targets the network namespace (not equestria) and uses wait:false with an explicit HelmRelease healthCheck, because the ipvlan-attached pod's readiness is judged by the HR rather than by generic resource readiness.

nodes.label: Static private key pinned by DANE TLSA
nodes.norm_label: static private key pinned by dane tlsa
nodes.rationale: privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never. The Technitium cluster's DANE TLSA records pin the SPKI hash, so a rotated key silently breaks node-to-node heartbeats — the failure is invisible at renewal time and only shows up as cluster desync.

nodes.label: Control-plane pinning via technitium-dns nodeLabel
nodes.rationale: nodeSelector technitium-dns=true moved off hard-hat 2026-08-19 onto milky-way/othalla/pegasus so the LAN resolver survives a low-power window with every worker off. The control-plane NoSchedule toleration is mandatory — a nodeSelector matching only tainted nodes without it yields an unschedulable pod.

nodes.label: exec-based health probes (127.0.0.1:5380)
nodes.rationale: tcpSocket probes are dialed by the kubelet from the node's LAN IP, but the pod answers out the ipvlan net1 interface — asymmetric routing means they always time out, the pod never goes Ready, and every Service loses its endpoints. Bash /dev/tcp exec probes run inside the pod and dodge the routing entirely.

nodes.label: Tier-1 longhorn-critical storage selection

Migrated from the component's longhorn default 2026-08-19 via the piece-13 choreography (final sync, RD restore, PVC recreate).

nodes.label: ExternalSecret ${APP}-volsync
nodes.rationale: Templates the restic repository credential Secret ${APP}-volsync-secret from the openbao ClusterSecretStore at apps/volsync/password (formerly the 1Password item 'Volsync Password' in vault Eris). RESTIC_REPOSITORY is derived per app as /repository/${APP} inside the shared mount, so each app gets its own restic repository. Carries reloader.stakater.com/auto so movers pick up a rotated password.

nodes.label: volsync Component
nodes.rationale: Bundles the four objects that make up an app's backup and restore path and stamps app.kubernetes.io/name, driscoll.dev/name and kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/force: enabled as commonLabels on all of them.

nodes.label: PersistentVolumeClaim ${APP}
nodes.rationale: The app's real data volume, provisioned through the VolSync volume populator via dataSourceRef -> ReplicationDestination/${APP}-dst so a first deploy restores from the latest restic snapshot instead of starting empty. Storage class is VOLSYNC_STORAGECLASS (default longhorn) — deliberately distinct from the mover's staging class since 2026-08-19.

nodes.label: ReplicationDestination ${APP}-dst
nodes.rationale: Restores the app's latest restic snapshot into a staging volume ${APP}-dst-dest that the app PVC then clones from. Uses its own VOLSYNC_STAGING_STORAGECLASS so restore churn can stay off a pinned tier. Cache default is 8Gi here versus 2Gi on the source — the asymmetry is why VOLSYNC_CACHE_CAPACITY should be pinned explicitly rather than inherited.

nodes.label: volsync component contract
nodes.rationale: The component provides the steady-state backup path: the ExternalSecret holding the restic repository credential, the nightly ReplicationSource, the app's PVC, and (since 639a049d) the ReplicationDestination. Consumers are Flux Kustomization CRs in the cluster repos referencing ../kubernetes/components/volsync via GitRepository/home-operations, so the references are invisible to a git grep inside this repo — search the cluster repos or query the live cluster before assuming a component is unused.

nodes.label: VOLSYNC_CAPACITY only ever goes up
nodes.rationale: Two one-way constraints fire together. resources.requests.storage is immutable downward, and with the kustomize force: enabled stamp Flux resolves the rejected patch by deleting the bound PVC and creating a new one. The replacement then cannot bind, because a snapshot cannot be restored into a volume smaller than its RESTORESIZE — still the old larger capacity. The symptom names neither cause: the app PVC and a vs-prime-* PVC both sit Pending forever with only 'assuming an external populator will provision the volume'. Recovery is to put the number back. Shipped once: #1084 cut forgejo 20Gi to 10Gi, Flux deleted the bound PVC within the minute, #1100 put it back; data loss was nil only because the forge's real state was in Postgres.

nodes.label: First-deploy volume populator trap
nodes.rationale: dataSourceRef is consulted only when a PVC is first created and is immutable and inert once Bound. On a brand-new PVC the VolSync populator claims it, Longhorn stands down ('assuming an external populator will provision the volume'), and the populator waits forever for a ReplicationDestination nothing creates — PVC Pending, no Longhorn volume, no obvious error (equestria-cluster#2987, stargate-command-cluster#1739). Shipping the destination unconditionally is what lets a first deploy or a forced PVC recreate bind on its own. Do not try to fix a stuck PVC by editing pvc.yaml: dataSourceRef is immutable and the populator re-enqueues unbound PVCs, so creating the ReplicationDestination is sufficient.

nodes.label: kustomize force: enabled stamp hazard
nodes.rationale: kustomization.yaml stamps kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/force: enabled on every resource in the component, so changing an immutable PVC field (storageClassName, dataSourceRef, or lowering requests.storage) makes Flux delete and recreate the PVC, destroying the data. Expanding VOLSYNC_CAPACITY is safe; changing storage class or lowering capacity is not.

nodes.label: Nightly destination rebuild cycle
nodes.rationale: spec.trigger.manual: restore-once fires once per destination; the volsync-restore-cleanup CronJob (30 3 * * *) deletes every destination whose status.lastManualSync caught up, cascading to its ${APP}-dst-dest/${APP}-dst-cache pair. Because the destination is declared in the component, Flux recreates it and the restore runs again — so every app performs a real restic restore at ~04:0x nightly. Measured 2026-08-24: 90 destination and cache volumes, 64.5 GiB restored, 124.4 GiB of Longhorn capacity with replicas. This is the same delete/recreate loop the 2026-07 Longhorn storage incident was traced to; 639a049d merged the split component back and recorded no rationale, so whether the nightly restore is an accepted cost of first-deploy safety or an unnoticed regression is written down nowhere. Treat as unresolved.

nodes.label: Pin the data, not the churn
nodes.norm_label: pin the data, not the churn
nodes.rationale: VOLSYNC_STORAGECLASS (default longhorn) controls the app's real data PVC; VOLSYNC_STAGING_STORAGECLASS (default longhorn-snapshot) the mover's throwaway staging clone and ${APP}-dst-dest; VOLSYNC_CACHE_SNAPSHOTCLASS (default longhorn-cache, misnamed — it is a storage class) the restic metadata cache. These were ONE variable until 2026-08-19, which is how the piece-12 Tier-1 migration put longhorn-critical on home-assistant's backup staging volume and cloned the full dataset onto three control-plane SATA disks at 3 replicas nightly. Exception: Tier 1 apps must point staging AND cache at longhorn-critical-snapshot/longhorn-critical-cache together, because Piece 12 Phase 5 restricts the default scratch classes to `bulk` and a Tier-1 app would have zero schedulable nodes while workers are powered down. Longhorn tag selectors are a hard filter with no preference order, so the choice is binary. Changing either staging variable is safe on a live app; changing VOLSYNC_STORAGECLASS on a bound PVC is not.

nodes.rationale: Both gRPC (4317) and HTTP (4318) OTLP endpoints are bound to 0.0.0.0 so any in-cluster workload can ship traces without a collector hop.

nodes.label: Thanos objstore.yml S3 template
nodes.rationale: Keys are rewritten with a minio_ prefix so a flat 1Password/OpenBao item maps onto the type: s3 objstore schema; insecure: true because Minio is reached over plain HTTP inside the cluster.

nodes.label: Thanos Compactor component
nodes.rationale: Retention ladder 7d raw / 90d 5m / 180d 1h trades resolution for bucket size as data ages.

nodes.label: Thanos Query component
nodes.rationale: dnsDiscovery points at prometheus-operated in observability so it federates the local Prometheus sidecars; replicaLabel __replica__ dedupes HA pairs.

nodes.label: Thanos Query Frontend component
nodes.rationale: Caching layer that Grafana and the public thanos.${ROOT_DOMAIN} ingress talk to, fronted by the network-authenticated-user Traefik middleware.

nodes.label: Thanos Receive component
nodes.rationale: Standalone remote-write sink with 10d TSDB retention on an 80Gi PVC, exposed to the tailnet via tailscale.com/expose + proxy-group so off-cluster Prometheis can push in.

nodes.label: Thanos Ruler component
nodes.rationale: Evaluates global rules over the whole query view rather than one Prometheus; dnsDiscovery disabled and queries pinned to the thanos-query Service, alerts routed to alertmanager-operated.

nodes.label: Thanos Store Gateway component
nodes.rationale: Serves historical blocks out of object storage; 10Gi longhorn PVC is index cache only, not the data itself.

nodes.label: Alert: OomKilled
nodes.rationale: Correlates a restart-count increase with a last-terminated-reason of OOMKilled to avoid firing on ordinary crash loops.

nodes.label: Rule group: PrometheusWatcher
nodes.rationale: Lives in Thanos rather than Prometheus on purpose - a rule that alerts when Prometheus is down cannot be evaluated by Prometheus itself.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: speedtest-exporter
nodes.rationale: Deployed from the shared bjw-s app-template OCIRepository rather than a bespoke chart; rollback remediation with 3 retries keeps a bad image from wedging the release.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: speedtest-exporter
nodes.rationale: dependsOn prometheus/observability so the ServiceMonitor and PrometheusRule CRDs exist before this path is applied.

nodes.label: PrometheusRule: speedtest-exporter-rules
nodes.rationale: Thresholds are hand-tuned to the 300/50 Mbps home line and evaluated over a 4h average because the exporter is scraped only hourly.

nodes.label: ServiceMonitor: speedtest-exporter
nodes.rationale: 60m interval with a 1m scrape timeout because each scrape actually runs a speedtest; the pod label is dropped so series survive pod churn.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: tempo
nodes.rationale: Single-binary Grafana Tempo with reporting disabled; install remediation retries are unbounded (-1) so a slow first PVC bind eventually succeeds.

nodes.label: OCIRepository: tempo chart
nodes.rationale: Chart pulled straight from oci://ghcr.io/grafana/helm-charts at a pinned tag rather than a HelmRepository index.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Thanos Query
nodes.rationale: Estate-local driscoll.dev/v1 CRD that drives authentik forward-auth, the dashboard tile and the Gatus check from one declaration. skipPathRegex ^/api keeps the Thanos HTTP API reachable behind forward_single proxy auth.

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: thanos-objstore
nodes.rationale: Pulls the Minio S3 credentials from OpenBao at clusters/equestria/apps/thanos/s3 and renders them into an objstore.yml the chart consumes via existingObjstoreSecret. deletionPolicy Retain keeps the bucket config if the source key vanishes.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: thanos
nodes.rationale: Bitnami chart with global.security.allowInsecureImages so the upstream quay.io/thanos/thanos image can replace the Bitnami one; priorityClassName observability-critical keeps it resident under pressure.

nodes.label: speedtest-exporter control-plane toleration (Tier 1)
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 per docs/cluster-consolidation/24 §1: the exporter must keep running during Battery mode, so it tolerates the control-plane NoSchedule taint. app-template renders controllers.<name>.pod.tolerations straight into the pod spec. Added after §8 Stage 2.

nodes.label: Tempo local trace backend
nodes.rationale: backend: local on a 10Gi PVC instead of object storage - traces are low-value/short-lived here, so the operational cost of an S3 bucket is not worth paying.

nodes.label: Tempo control-plane toleration
nodes.rationale: Chart exposes one top-level tolerations key. This is placement flexibility only: Tempo is a StatefulSet with a 10Gi PVC, so the toleration widens where it MAY schedule without moving its data.

nodes.label: Orphan deletion policy (migration churn)
nodes.rationale: deletionPolicy: Orphan so that Kustomization churn during the cluster consolidation does not delete live workloads/PVCs. See docs/cluster-consolidation/27-migration-churn-failure-modes.md.

nodes.label: Per-component control-plane tolerations
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 per 24 §1 (observability stays up during Battery). bitnami/thanos exposes ONE tolerations key per component - there is no global one - so every enabled component must repeat the same control-plane toleration. Added after §8 Stage 2. See docs/cluster-consolidation/20-low-power-tier.md §4.

nodes.label: prowlarr-log CNPG Database
nodes.rationale: Must exist before the pod does: with DBENABLED on, the app connects to PostgresLogDb at startup and will not create it (Bootstrap.cs otherwise calls AddDummyLogDatabase). Uses the app's own role and credential; databaseReclaimPolicy retain because ensure: absent would DROP the database - deleting the file is the safe way to stop managing it.

nodes.label: TECHNITIUM_VIP static LAN address on net1
nodes.norm_label: technitium_vip static lan address on net1
nodes.rationale: DNS traffic (53 UDP/TCP, 853 DoT, 443 DoH) lands directly on the dedicated interface, bypassing kube-proxy and any LoadBalancer service; the /16 broadcast domain means the same address is valid on either parent NIC.

nodes.label: emberstack reflector secret mirroring
nodes.rationale: The Secret carries no data of its own; it is filled by reflector from tailscale-system/tailscale-dns-authkey, whose source carries reflection-allowed=true.

nodes.label: Autobrr Authentik confidential OAuth2 client
nodes.rationale: Autobrr speaks OIDC natively, so it gets a real confidential OAuth2 client with two redirect URIs (public domain and tailnet domain) rather than the forward-auth proxy used by the Servarr-family apps in this directory.

nodes.label: postgres_ / oidc_ dataFrom rewrite pipeline
nodes.rationale: Two regexp steps normalise hyphenated credential keys into legal Go template identifiers and then namespace them. The credential Secret's key is `username`, so the template must say .postgres_username; .postgres_user renders empty and lib/pq silently falls back to the OS user (uid 568, no passwd entry), failing at connect time with a misleading error.

nodes.label: PROWLARR__LOG__DBENABLED toggle
nodes.rationale: Set to "True" now that the log database exists; it restores System > Logs in the UI and simultaneously makes the log database REQUIRED at startup. Flipping it back to "False" is the rollback if that database is ever missing.

nodes.label: bittorrent LoadBalancer service (TCP+UDP 18289)
nodes.rationale: A second Service on a pinned loadBalancerIP carries the torrenting port on both protocols, separate from the ClusterIP WebUI service that the Gateway routes to; UPnP is disabled because the address is assigned statically.

nodes.label: enp3s0 control-plane NIC as ipvlan master
nodes.norm_label: enp3s0 control-plane nic as ipvlan master
nodes.rationale: Changed from enp2s0 (worker NIC) on 2026-08-19 to move Technitium onto the control planes for low-power / battery mode; requires the technitium-dns=true node label set from talos/talconfig.yaml plus a matching pod nodeSelector.

nodes.label: ipvlan L2 instead of macvlan on Proxmox KVM nodes
nodes.norm_label: ipvlan l2 instead of macvlan on proxmox kvm nodes
nodes.rationale: macvlan would require promiscuous mode on the Proxmox vmbr bridge; ipvlan L2 shares the parent MAC so no Proxmox reconfiguration is needed.

nodes.label: Nightly Low Power Gatus maintenance window
nodes.norm_label: nightly low power gatus maintenance window
nodes.rationale: The service is scaled to 0 between 02:00 and 09:00 by the nightly power shed, so a failed check in that window is expected. Gatus keeps checking and keeps the history but does not alert.

nodes.label: AUTOBRR__DATABASE_TYPE silent Postgres switch
nodes.rationale: internal/config/config.go gates the env value behind validDatabaseType, so a missing or invalid type is dropped silently and autobrr stays on SQLite with every POSTGRES_* var set and nothing logged. A bad databaseType in config.toml is ungated and hard-errors instead.

nodes.label: Default secretStoreRef corrected off onepassword-connect
nodes.rationale: Every dataFrom carries an explicit sourceRef so the default store was never consulted; it named onepassword-connect purely by template inheritance. Pointing it at the store actually in use removes a phantom 1Password dependency.

nodes.label: Brand-new-app Postgres role race
nodes.rationale: autobrr had no database or role in the cluster when components/postgres was enabled (2026-08-26), so stacks/system creates the OpenBao static role before CNPG applies the DatabaseRole and stalls on 'role "autobrr" does not exist'. Expected; recovery documented in components/postgres/ks.yaml and the runbook.

nodes.label: PROWLARR__SECTION__KEY prefix spelled out by hand
nodes.norm_label: prowlarr__section__key prefix spelled out by hand
nodes.rationale: The credential Secret's key names do not match the app's env var names and the upper-case prefix is not derivable from ${APP} (kustomize has no upper-case function), so each app spells its own five keys out instead of passing dataFrom straight through.

nodes.label: PROWLARR__POSTGRES__HOST as the Postgres on-switch
nodes.rationale: Sonarr-family apps use Postgres if and only if PostgresHost is non-empty (NzbDrone.Core/Datastore/ConnectionStringFactory.cs). Removing this ExternalSecret and its envFrom drops the app back onto the SQLite file still sitting in the config PVC - which is the rollback, and why that file is not deleted.

nodes.label: One credential, two databases (main + log)
nodes.rationale: ConnectionStringFactory builds both connections from the same PostgresUser/Password/Host/Port and varies only the database name, so there is no second role, no second OpenBao static role and no second password. LOGDB is a literal because the credential Secret describes only one database.

nodes.label: Startup probe buys migration time (prowlarr)
nodes.rationale: Same ~110s liveness budget problem as autobrr: an empty-Postgres first boot replays the entire migration chain and the 30-day rotation forces cold starts. 60 x 10s startup checks suspend liveness and readiness and cost nothing on a normal boot that answers /ping immediately.

nodes.label: postgres-databases deliberately excluded from the app build
nodes.norm_label: postgres-databases deliberately excluded from the app build
nodes.rationale: The directory sits inside the app's build path, so listing it in ../kustomization.yaml would render the Database a second time into the equestria namespace, where it is meaningless (CNPG resolves spec.cluster.name locally) and would fight the real one in the database namespace.

nodes.label: Log database backup opt-out annotation
nodes.rationale: driscoll.dev/backup is an opt-OUT here (opt-IN for a Garage bucket) because the stakes differ. The database holds only app log entries that Prowlarr trims itself. backup-credentials is set as belt and braces: flipping the flag would otherwise send the backup looking for ${APP}-log-postgres, which does not exist, and one failed database exits the whole nightly job non-zero.

nodes.label: public-only schema avoids $user shadowing
nodes.rationale: A schema named after the role arms the dormant $user element of the default search_path and shadows public, so only the public schema is declared.

nodes.label: MemoryWorkingSetLimit derived from the container limit
nodes.norm_label: memoryworkingsetlimit derived from the container limit
nodes.rationale: QBT_Application__MemoryWorkingSetLimit is fed by a resourceFieldRef on limits.memory with a 1Mi divisor, so qBittorrent's own cache ceiling tracks the Kubernetes memory limit automatically instead of being a second number to keep in sync.

nodes.label: Tandoor Startup Probe Cold-Boot Window
nodes.rationale: A cold boot is nginx -> wait for DB -> migrate -> collectstatic -> gunicorn, and collectstatic re-hashes every static file on every start (~2m40s measured). Liveness only allows 40s, so without a startup probe the container is killed mid-collectstatic and crash-loops instead of converging (observed 2026-08-25 during the tranche-3 password rotation: 6 restarts, though the credential was never the problem). Liveness/readiness timeouts were also widened from 1s to 5s because a timed-out probe counts as a FAILED probe (the `499` in the access log) and three of them killed the container. A pending startup probe suppresses liveness and readiness, so this only widens the boot window and leaves steady-state behaviour untouched.

nodes.rationale: Control-plane toleration is documented in-file as placement flexibility ONLY: Alertmanager is a StatefulSet on a 1Gi Longhorn PVC, so a toleration widens where it MAY schedule but the pod still follows its volume.
